p0.original: The revenue which must defray, not only the expense of defending the society and of supporting the dignity of the chief magistrate, but all the other necessary expenses of government, for which the constitution of the state has not provided any particular revenue may be drawn, either, first, from some fund which peculiarly belongs to the sovereign or commonwealth, and which is independent of the revenue of the people; or, secondly, from the revenue of the people.
p0.zh: 必须支付的收入,不仅用于捍卫社会和支持首席治安法官尊严的费用,而且用于政府所有其他必要的开支,国家宪法没有为此提供任何特定收入,这些开支可以首先从一些特殊属于主权或联邦、独立于人民收入的基金中提取;其次,也可以从人民收入中提取。

p1.original: PART I. Of the Funds, or Sources, of Revenue, which may peculiarly belong to the Sovereign or Commonwealth.
p1.zh: 第一编属于主权或联邦的专项收入基金或收入来源。

p2.original: The funds, or sources, of revenue, which may peculiarly belong to the sovereign or commonwealth, must consist, either in stock, or in land.
p2.zh: 收入的资金或来源,可能特别属于主权或联邦,必须库存或土地组成。

p3.original: The sovereign, like, any other owner of stock, may derive a revenue from it, either by employing it himself, or by lending it. His revenue is, in the one case, profit, in the other interest.
p3.zh: 主权者,如任何其他股票所有者,可以从中获取收入,无论是通过自己使用,还是通过借出. 他的收入,在一种情况下,是利润,在另一种利益。

p4.original: The revenue of a Tartar or Arabian chief consists in profit. It arises principally from the milk and increase of his own herds and flocks, of which he himself superintends the management, and is the principal shepherd or herdsman of his own horde or tribe. It is, however, in this earliest and rudest state of civil government only, that profit has ever made the principal part of the public revenue of a monarchical state.
p4.zh: 鞑靼人或阿拉伯酋长的收入为利润。 这主要源于他自己的牧群和羊群的牛奶和增殖,而他本人则在其中占据管理权,并且是他自己部落或部落的主要牧羊人或牧民。 然而,正是在这种最早和最粗鲁的民政府状态下,利润曾经成为君主制国家公共收入的主要部分.

p5.original: Small republics have sometimes derived a considerable revenue from the profit of mercantile projects. The republic of Hamburgh is said to do so from the profits of a public wine-cellar and apothecary's shop. {See Memoires concernant les Droits et Impositions en Europe, tome i. page 73. This work was compiled by the order of the court, for the use of a commission employed for some years past in considering the proper means for reforming the finances of France. The account of the French taxes, which takes up three volumes in quarto, may be regarded as perfectly authentic. That of those of other European nations was compiled from such information as the French ministers at the different courts could procure. It is much shorter, and probably not quite so exact as that of the French taxes.} That state cannot be very great, of which the sovereign has leisure to carry on the trade of a wine-merchant or an apothecary. The profit of a public bank has been a source of revenue to more considerable states. It has been so, not only to Hamburgh, but to Venice and Amsterdam. A revenue of this kind has even by some people been thought not below the attention of so great an empire as that of Great Britain. Reckoning the ordinary dividend of the bank of England at five and a-half per cent., and its capital at ten millions seven hundred and eighty thousand pounds, the neat annual profit, after paying the expense of management, must amount, it is said, to five hundred and ninety-two thousand nine hundred pounds. Government, it is pretended, could borrow this capital at three per cent. interest, and, by taking the management of the bank into its own hands, might make a clear profit of two hundred and sixty-nine thousand five hundred pounds a-year. The orderly, vigilant, and parsimonious administration of such aristocracies as those of Venice and Amsterdam, is extremely proper, it appears from experience, for the management of a mercantile project of this kind. But whether such a government us that of England, which, whatever may be its virtues, has never been famous for good economy; which, in time of peace, has generally conducted itself with the slothful and negligent profusion that is, perhaps, natural to monarchies; and, in time of war, has constantly acted with all the thoughtless extravagance that democracies are apt to fall into, could be safely trusted with the management of such a project, must at least be a good deal more doubtful.
p5.zh: 小的共和国有时从商贸项目的利润中获得了相当可观的收入.汉堡共和国据说利用一家公共酒馆和药店的利润这样做。 {见《欧洲人权和立场备忘录》,第73页。这项工作是根据法院的命令汇编的,以便利用过去几年来在考虑改革法国财政的适当手段时所使用的一个委员会。 法国税收的核算用夸尔托语分三卷,可以认为是完全真实的. 其他欧洲国家的这种资料是根据法国部长在不同法院可能获得的资料汇编的。 它短得多,而且可能不象法国的税收那么精确。 ” 这个国家不可能是一个非常伟大的国家,其中君主可以闲暇地从事酒商或药剂师的贸易。公共银行的利润一直是相当大一些州的收入来源。 它一直如此,不仅是汉堡,还有威尼斯和阿姆斯特丹. 甚至有些人认为,这种收入不低于大不列颠帝国的注意力。估计英国银行的普通股息为5%半,其资本为1千万780万英磅,整洁的年利润,在支付管理费后,必须达到592万9百英磅. 政府,它假装,可以以3%的利率借来这笔资本,利息,通过自己掌握银行的管理权,可以使每年有269,500英镑的利润明显增加。 从经验来看,对威尼斯和阿姆斯特丹等贵族的有序、警惕和冷酷的管理,对于管理这种商业项目是极为恰当的。 但是,我们英格兰的这样一个政府,无论它有什么优点,是否从未以良好的经济而闻名;在和平时期,它一般是用也许对君主国来说自然而然的懒惰和疏忽的流水来表现的;在战争时期,它是否经常用民主国家可能陷入的不思议的奢侈行为来采取行动,在管理这样一个项目时,它是否能够被安全地信任,至少是更令人怀疑的好东西。

p6.original: The post-office is properly a mercantile project. The government advances the expense of establishing the different offices, and of buying or hiring the necessary horses or carriages, and is repaid, with a large profit, by the duties upon what is carried. It is, perhaps, the only mercantile project which has been successfully managed by, I believe, every sort of government. The capital to be advanced is not very considerable. There is no mystery in the business. The returns are not only certain but immediate.
p6.zh: 后台是一个商贸项目。 政府垫付设立不同办事处的费用,以及购买或雇用必要的马匹或马车的费用,并用所携带的军费偿还,利润巨大。这可能是我所相信的 每一个类型的政府都成功管理的唯一商业项目。有待推进的首都规模不大.生意上没有神秘之处返回不仅是确定的,而且是立即的。

p7.original: Princes, however, have frequently engaged in many other mercantile projects, and have been willing, like private persons, to mend their fortunes, by becoming adventurers in the common branches of trade. They have scarce ever succeeded. The profusion with which the affairs of princes are always managed, renders it almost impossible that they should. The agents of a prince regard the wealth of their master as inexhaustible; are careless at what price they buy, are careless at what price they sell, are careless at what expense they transport his goods from one place to another. Those agents frequently live with the profusion of princes; and sometimes, too, in spite of that profusion, and by a proper method of making up their accounts, acquire the fortunes of princes. It was thus, as we are told by Machiavel, that the agents of Lorenzo of Medicis, not a prince of mean abilities, carried on his trade. The republic of Florence was several times obliged to pay the debt into which their extravagance had involved him. He found it convenient, accordingly to give up the business of merchant, the business to which his family had originally owed their fortune, and, in the latter part of his life, to employ both what remained of that fortune, and the revenue of the state, of which he had the disposal, in projects and expenses more suitable to his station.
p7.zh: 然而,王子们经常参与许多其他的商贸项目,并且像私人一样,愿意通过成为共同贸易分支中的冒险者来弥补自己的财富. 他们几乎没有成功过。王子的事务总是由他们管理,使他们几乎不可能这样做。王子的代理人认为主人的财富是不可穷尽的;他们不小心地以什么价格购买,他们不小心地以什么价格出售,他们不小心地将他的商品从一个地方运送到另一个地方。 这些特工经常与大量王子一起生活;有时,尽管如此,他们还是通过适当的方法,以适当的方法来编造他们的账户,获得王子的财富。 因此,正如马奇雅维尔告诉我们的那样,美第奇斯的洛伦佐的特工们,而不是一个能力低下的王子,继续从事他的生意。佛罗伦萨共和国多次被迫偿还他们外出债务。 因此,他认为放弃商人的生意是方便的,他的家人原来欠他们的财富的生意,在后半辈子,他既要利用那份财富的剩余部分,又要利用他处理的州的收入,进行项目,并支付更适合他站点的开支.

p8.original: No two characters seem more inconsistent than those of trader and sovereign. If the trading spirit of the English East India company renders them very bad sovereigns, the spirit of sovereignty seems to have rendered them equally bad traders. While they were traders only, they managed their trade successfully, and were able to pay from their profits a moderate dividend to the proprietors of their stock. Since they became sovereigns, with a revenue which, it is said, was originally more than three millions sterling, they have been obliged to beg the ordinary assistance of government, in order to avoid immediate bankruptcy. In their former situation, their servants in India considered themselves as the clerks of merchants; in their present situation, those servants consider themselves as the ministers of sovereigns.
p8.zh: 似乎没有两个角色比商人和主权角色更不一致。 如果英属东印度公司的贸易精神使他们变得非常糟糕的君主,那么主权精神似乎也使他们同样糟糕的商人. 虽然他们只是贸易商,但他们成功地管理了他们的贸易,能够从利润中向股票的所有人支付适度的红利。 自从他们成为君主以来,由于收入据说原来超过300万英镑,他们不得不向政府乞求一般援助,以避免立即破产。其在印度的仆人曾认为自己是商人的书记官;在目前的情况下,这些仆人认为自己是君主的大臣.

p9.original: A state may sometimes derive some part of its public revenue from the interest of money, as well as from the profits of stock. If it has amassed a treasure, it may lend a part of that treasure, either to foreign states, or to its own subjects.
p9.zh: 国家有时可能从金钱利息和股票利润中获取部分公共收入。 如果它积聚了宝藏,它可能会把一部分宝藏借给外国或自己的臣民.

p10.original: The canton of Berne derives a considerable revenue by lending a part of its treasure to foreign states, that is, by placing it in the public funds of the different indebted nations of Europe, chiefly in those of France and England. The security of this revenue must depend, first, upon the security of the funds in which it is placed, or upon the good faith of the government which has the management of them; and, secondly, upon the certainty or probability of the continuance of peace with the debtor nation. In the case of a war, the very first act of hostility on the part of the debtor nation might be the forfeiture of the funds of its credit. This policy of lending money to foreign states is, so far as I know peculiar to the canton of Berne.
p10.zh: 伯尔尼州通过向外国借出一部分财富,即将其存入欧洲不同债务国的公共资金,主要是法国和英国的公款,获得可观的收入。这笔收入的安全首先必须取决于所存资金的安全,或者取决于管理这些资金的政府是否有诚意;其次,必须取决于与债务国继续和平的确定性或概率。 在战争的情况下,债务国的第一个敌对行为可能是没收其信贷资金。 这种向外国贷款的政策, 据我所知,是伯尔尼州特有的。

p11.original: The city of Hamburgh {See Memoire concernant les Droites et Impositions en Europe tome i p. 73.}has established a sort of public pawn-shop, which lends money to the subjects of the state, upon pledges, at six per cent. interest. This pawn-shop, or lombard, as it is called, affords a revenue, it is pretended, to the state, of a hundred and fifty thousand crowns, which, at four and sixpence the crown, amounts to £33,750 sterling.
p11.zh: 汉堡市{见关于欧洲人权和立场的备忘录 i p.73. 已经建立了一种公共当铺,向国家主体贷款,认捐时利率为6%。 这个当铺,或称隆巴德,可以提供一笔收入,它被假扮成,州里有十万五万的王冠,在四六便士的王冠上,相当于33,750英镑.

p12.original: The government of Pennsylvania, without amassing any treasure, invented a method of lending, not money, indeed, but what is equivalent to money, to its subjects. By advancing to private people, at interest, and upon land security to double the value, paper bills of credit, to be redeemed fifteen years after their date; and, in the mean time, made transferable from hand to hand, like banknotes, and declared by act of assembly to be a legal tender in all payments from one inhabitant of the province to another, it raised a moderate revenue, which went a considerable way towards defraying an annual expense of about £4,500, the whole ordinary expense of that frugal and orderly government. The success of an expedient of this kind must have depended upon three different circumstances: first, upon the demand for some other instrument of commerce, besides gold and silver money, or upon the demand for such a quantity of consumable stock as could not be had without sending abroad the greater part of their gold and silver money, in order to purchase it; secondly, upon the good credit of the government which made use of this expedient; and, thirdly, upon the moderation with which it was used, the whole value of the paper bills of credit never exceeding that of the gold and silver money which would have been necessary for carrying on their circulation, had there been no paper bills of credit. The same expedient was, upon different occasions, adopted by several other American colonies; but, from want of this moderation, it produced, in the greater part of them, much more disorder than conveniency.
p12.zh: 宾夕法尼亚州政府,没有积累任何财宝,就发明了一种借给臣民的方法,不是金钱,而是相当于金钱的东西. 通过向私人、利息和土地担保提供价值翻一番的纸质信用证,在日期之后15年后予以赎回;在短短的时间里,纸质信用证如同纸币一样,从手到手可转移,并通过集会法宣布,该省居民向另一居民支付的所有款项都是法定的,它筹集了适度的收入,大大促进了每年支付约4 500英镑的开支,这是这一节俭有序的政府的全部一般开支。 这种权宜之计能否成功,必须取决于三种不同的情况:第一,除了金银钱以外,还需要其他某种商业工具,或者需要这样数量的消耗性库存,而如果不将其金银钱的较大部分汇往国外购买,则无法做到;第二,需要利用这种权宜之计的政府的良好信誉;第三,如果没有纸面信用证,纸面信用证的全部价值就永远不能超过其流通所必需的金银钱的价值。同样的权宜之计在不同场合被其他几个美国殖民地所采纳;但是,由于缺乏这种温和,在它们中的大部分地区,它制造的混乱比收缩多得多。

p13.original: The unstable and perishable nature of stock and credit, however, renders them unfit to be trusted to as the principal funds of that sure, steady, and permanent revenue, which can alone give security and dignity to government. The government of no great nation, that was advanced beyond the shepherd state, seems ever to have derived the greater part of its public revenue from such sources.
p13.zh: 然而,股票和信贷的不稳定和易腐烂性质使它们不适于被信任为这种可靠、稳定和永久收入的本金,而只有这种收入才能给政府带来安全和尊严。超越牧羊国的伟大国家政府似乎从这些来源获得其大部分公共收入。

p14.original: Land is a fund of more stable and permanent nature; and the rent of public lands, accordingly, has been the principal source of the public revenue of many a great nation that was much advanced beyond the shepherd state. From the produce or rent of the public lands, the ancient republics of Greece and Italy derived for a long the the greater part of that revenue which defrayed the necessary expenses of the commonwealth. The rent of the crown lands constituted for a long time the greater part of the revenue of the ancient sovereigns of Europe.
p14.zh: 土地是更加稳定和永久性质的基金;因此,公共土地的租金一直是许多伟大国家公共收入的主要来源,而这一国家已经超越牧羊国。长期以来,希腊和意大利的古代共和国从公共土地的产地或租地中获取了大部分收入,以支付联邦的必要开支。长期以来,皇冠土地的租金是欧洲古代君主收入的较大部分。

p15.original: War, and the preparation for war, are the two circumstances which, in modern times, occasion the greater part of the necessary expense or all great states. But in the ancient republics of Greece and Italy, every citizen was a soldier, and both served, and prepared himself for service, at his own expense. Neither of those two circumstances, therefore, could occasion any very considerable expense to the state. The rent of a very moderate landed estate might be fully sufficient for defraying all the other necessary expenses of government.
p15.zh: 战争和战争的准备是两种情况,在现代,它们造成大部分必要的开支或所有大国。 但在古代希腊和意大利的共和国,每个公民都是军人,他们都服务,并准备服役,自费. 因此,这两种情况都不可能给国家带来任何巨大的开支。 一个非常温和的地产的租金可能足以支付政府所有其他必要的开支。

p16.original: In the ancient monarchies of Europe, the manners and customs of the time sufficiently prepared the great body of the people for war; and when they took the field, they were, by the condition of their feudal tenures, to be maintained either at their own expense, or at that of their immediate lords, without bringing any new charge upon the sovereign. The other expenses of government were, the greater part of them, very moderate. The administration of justice, it has been shewn, instead of being a cause of expense was a source of revenue. The labour of the country people, for three days before, and for three days after, harvest, was thought a fund sufficient for making and maintaining all the bridges, highways, and other public works, which the commerce of the country was supposed to require. In those days the principal expense of the sovereign seems to have consisted in the maintenance of his own family and household. The officers of his household, accordingly, were then the great officers of state. The lord treasurer received his rents. The lord steward and lord chamberlain looked after the expense of his family. The care of his stables was committed to the lord constable and the lord marshal. His houses were all built in the form of castles, and seem to have been the principal fortresses which he possessed. The keepers of those houses or castles might be considered as a sort of military governors. They seem to have been the only military officers whom it was necessary to maintain in time of peace. In these circumstances, the rent of a great landed estate might, upon ordinary occasions, very well defray all the necessary expenses of government.
p16.zh: 在欧洲古代的君主制中,当时的礼仪和风俗,足以使人民的伟大身体备战;当他们夺取田地时,根据封建任期的条件,他们要么自费维持,要么直接领主维持,而不会给君主带来任何新的费用. 政府的其他开支是,大部分是,非常温和。司法行政一直被搁置,而不是作为开支的原因,而是收入来源。 全国人民的劳动,在收割前三天,在收割后三天,被认为是一个足以制造和维持全国商业应该需要的一切桥梁,高速公路,以及其他公共工程的基金. 在那些时候,君主的主要开支似乎包括维持自己的家庭。 因此,他的家庭官员是当时的国务大官。财主收其租.管家和长官负责照顾家人的费用。 他的马厩的护卫是献给治安官和治安官的。 他的房屋都是以城堡的形式建造的,似乎是他拥有的主要堡垒. 这些房屋或城堡的保管人可能被视为一种军事总督。 他们似乎是和平时期唯一需要维持的军官。 在这种情况下,在普通情况下,租用一个大地产可以很好地支付政府的所有必要费用。

p17.original: In the present state of the greater part of the civilized monarchies of Europe, the rent of all the lands in the country, managed as they probably would be, if they all belonged to one proprietor, would scarce, perhaps, amount to the ordinary revenue which they levy upon the people even in peaceable times. The ordinary revenue of Great Britain, for example, including not only what is necessary for defraying the current expense of the year, but for paying the interest of the public debts, and for sinking a part of the capital of those debts, amounts to upwards of ten millions a-year. But the land tax, at four shillings in the pound, falls short of two millions a-year. This land tax, as it is called however, is supposed to be one-fifth, not only of the rent of all the land, but of that of all the houses, and of the interest of all the capital stock of Great Britain, that part of it only excepted which is either lent to the public, or employed as farming stock in the cultivation of land. A very considerable part of the produce of this tax arises from the rent of houses and the interest of capital stock. The land tax of the city of London, for example, at four shillings in the pound, amounts to £123,399: 6: 7; that of the city of Westminster to £63,092: 1: 5; that of the palaces of Whitehall and St. James's, to £30,754: 6: 3. A certain proportion of the land tax is, in the same manner, assessed upon all the other cities and towns corporate in the kingdom; and arises almost altogether, either from the rent of houses, or from what is supposed to be the interest of trading and capital stock. According to the estimation, therefore, by which Great Britain is rated to the land tax, the whole mass of revenue arising from the rent of all the lands, from that of all the houses, and from the interest of all the capital stock, that part of it only excepted which is either lent to the public, or employed in the cultivation of land, does not exceed ten millions sterling a-year, the ordinary revenue which government levies upon the people, even in peaceable times. The estimation by which Great Britain is rated to the land tax is, no doubt, taking the whole kingdom at an average, very much below the real value; though in several particular counties and districts it is said to be nearly equal to that value. The rent of the lands alone, exclusive of that of houses and of the interest of stock, has by many people been estimated at twenty millions; an estimation made in a great measure at random, and which, I apprehend, is as likely to be above as below the truth. But if the lands of Great Britain, in the present state of their cultivation, do not afford a rent of more than twenty millions a-year, they could not well afford the half, most probably not the fourth part of that rent, if they all belonged to a single proprietor, and were put under the negligent, expensive, and oppressive management of his factors and agents. The crown lands of Great Britain do not at present afford the fourth part of the rent which could probably be drawn from them if they were the property of private persons. If the crown lands were more extensive, it is probable, they would be still worse managed.
p17.zh: 在欧洲大部分文明君主制国家的现状中,如果所有土地都属于一个所有者,那么,该国所有土地的租金就可能很少,也许相当于他们在和平时期向人民征收的普通收入。 例如,大不列颠的普通收入,不仅包括支付当年开支所必需的收入,而且包括支付公共债务利息和使部分债务资本沉没所必需的收入,每年超过1 000万美元。 但土地税,以英镑四先令计算,每年不足200万元. 但是,这种土地税,如它所说的,应该是五分之一,不仅涉及所有土地的租金,而且涉及所有房屋的租金,也涉及大不列颠所有资本存量的利益,除了一部分是借给公众的以外,或者作为农作储备用于土地的耕种。 这种税收的很大一部分来自房屋租金和资本库存利息。 例如,伦敦市的土地税以英镑4先令计,共计123,399英镑:6:7;威斯敏斯特市的土地税以63,092英镑计:1:5;怀特霍尔和圣塔的宫殿.詹姆斯的,到30,754英镑:6:3.土地税的一定比例以同样的方式对王国境内所有其他城镇公司进行评估;几乎全部来自房屋租金,或来自交易和资本存量的预期利益。 因此,根据对大不列颠征收土地税的估算,所有土地的租金、所有房屋的租金和所有资本存量的利息所产生的全部收入,只有部分除外,这些土地或是借给公众,或是用于耕种土地,每年不超过1 000万英镑,即政府向人民征收的普通收入,即使在和平时期也是如此。 毫无疑问,大不列颠被评为土地税的估计是将整个王国平均地,大大低于实际价值;虽然在几个特定的县和区,据说几乎等于实际价值。 据许多人估计,仅土地的租金,不包括房屋的租金和股权的租金,就达2 000万;这种估计在很大程度上是随机的,我认为,这种估计很可能高于事实。 但是,如果大不列颠的土地,在目前的种植状态下,每年负担不起超过两千万的租金,那么,如果它们都属于一个业主,并且被置于他的因素和代理人的疏忽、昂贵和压迫性管理之下,那么它们就负担不起一半的租金,最有可能不是第四部分的租金。 大不列颠的王室土地目前负担不起租金的第四部分,如果这些土地是私人财产,它们可能从中提取。 如果王冠土地面积更大,很可能,它们的管理会更加糟糕。

p18.original: The revenue which the great body of the people derives from land is, in proportion, not to the rent, but to the produce of the land. The whole annual produce of the land of every country, if we except what is reserved for seed, is either annually consumed by the great body of the people, or exchanged for something else that is consumed by them. Whatever keeps down the produce of the land below what it would otherwise rise to, keeps down the revenue of the great body of the people, still more than it does that of the proprietors of land. The rent of land, that portion of the produce which belongs to the proprietors, is scarce anywhere in Great Britain supposed to be more than a third part of the whole produce. If the land which, in one state of cultivation, affords a revenue of ten millions sterling a-year, would in another afford a rent of twenty millions; the rent being, in both cases, supposed a third part of the produce, the revenue of the proprietors would be less than it otherwise might be, by ten millions a-year only; but the revenue of the great hotly of the people would be less than it otherwise might be, by thirty millions a-year, deducting only what would be necessary for seed. The population of the country would be less by the number of people which thirty millions a-year, deducting always the seed, could maintain, according to the particular mode of living, and expense which might take place in the different ranks of men, among whom the remainder was distributed.
p18.zh: 人民大军从土地所得的收入,按比例,不归租界,而归土地之产.每个国家土地的整个年产,如果我们除了留给种子的东西外,不是每年被伟大的人民体消耗,就是交换他们消耗的其他东西. 凡使土地的产物低于它本来能产生的产物,则使人民的伟大身体的收入减少,比土地所有者的收入还要多。土地的租金,即属于业主的那部分产品,在大不列颠任何地方都很少,被认为是整个产品的三分之一以上。 如果在一种种植状态下每年能提供1 000万英镑收入的土地在另一种情况下能提供2 000万英镑的租金;在这两种情况下,租金都假定是产量的三分之一,那么业主的收入将比其他情况下少,每年仅减少1 000万加元;但是,最热的人民的收入将比其他情况下少,每年减少3 000万加元,只扣除种子所需的费用。 全国人口将少于每年3 000万人口的人数,而每年从种子中扣除,根据特定生活方式,可以维持这一人口数量,而不同阶层的男子可能承担费用,其余部分由男子分担。

p19.original: Though there is not at present in Europe, any civilized state of any kind which derives the greater part of its public revenue from the rent of lands which are the property of the state; yet, in all the great monarchies of Europe, there are still many large tracts of land which belong to the crown. They are generally forest, and sometimes forests where, after travelling several miles, you will scarce find a single tree; a mere waste and loss of country, in respect both of produce and population. In every great monarchy of Europe, the sale of the crown lands would produce a very large sum of money, which, if applied to the payment of the public debts, would deliver from mortgage a much greater revenue than any which those lands have even afforded to the crown. In countries where lands, improved and cultivated very highly, and yielding, at the time of sale, as great a rent as can easily be got from them, commonly sell at thirty years purchase; the unimproved, uncultivated, and low-rented crown lands, might well be expected to sell at forty, fifty, or sixty years purchase. The crown might immediately enjoy the revenue which this great price would redeem from mortgage. In the course of a few years, it would probably enjoy another revenue. When the crown lands had become private property, they would, in the course of a few years, become well improved and well cultivated. The increase of their produce would increase the population of the country, by augmenting the revenue and consumption of the people. But the revenue which the crown derives from the duties or custom and excise, would necessarily increase with the revenue and consumption of the people.
p19.zh: 尽管目前欧洲还没有任何文明国家,任何一种文明的国家,如果其公共收入的大部分来自作为国家财产的土地的租金;然而,在欧洲所有大君主国中,仍然有许多大片土地属于王冠。 它们一般是森林,有时是森林,在行走几英里后,你们将很少找到一棵树;就生产和人口而言,这只是浪费和丧失国家。在欧洲的每一个大君主国,出售王室土地都会产生非常大一笔钱,如果用于偿还公共债务,则从抵押中获得的收入将大大超过这些土地甚至给予王室的任何收入。 在那些土地在出售时改良和耕种非常高,而且收益丰厚的国家,其租金可以轻易地从这些土地中获取,通常在30年购买时出售;未改良、未耕种和低租的王冠土地,很可能预期在40年、50年或60年购买时出售。皇冠可能立即享受这一巨大价格从抵押中赎回的收入。 在几年内,它可能享有另外一笔收入。 当王冠土地成为私人财产时,它们将在几年内得到良好的改善和良好的耕种。增加他们的产量将增加人民的收入和消费,从而增加该国的人口。 但是,王室的收入来自关税或风俗和消费,随着人民的收入和消费,必然会增加。

p20.original: The revenue which, in any civilized monarchy, the crown derives from the crown lands, though it appears to cost nothing to individuals, in reality costs more to the society than perhaps any other equal revenue which the crown enjoys. It would, in all cases, be for the interest of the society, to replace this revenue to the crown by some other equal revenue, and to divide the lands among the people, which could not well be done better, perhaps, than by exposing them to public sale.
p20.zh: 在任何文明的君主制国家,王室的收入来自王室的土地,尽管它似乎并不给个人带来任何代价,但实际上,社会付出的代价可能比王室享有的任何其他同等收入要高。在所有情况下,都是为了社会的利益,用一些其他平等收入来取代这种收入,并在人民中划分土地,这或许比将他们公开出售更能做得更好。

p21.original: Lands, for the purposes of pleasure and magnificence, parks, gardens, public walks, etc. possessions which are everywhere considered as causes of expense, not as sources of revenue, seem to be the only lands which, in a great and civilized monarchy, ought to belong to the crown.
p21.zh: 土地,为了愉悦和放大的目的,公园,花园,公共散步等财产,在任何地方都被认为是开支的原因,而不是收入来源,似乎是在伟大和文明的君主制中,唯一应该属于王冠的土地.

p22.original: Public stock and public lands, therefore, the two sources of revenue which may peculiarly belong to the sovereign or commonwealth, being both improper and insufficient funds for defraying the necessary expense of any great and civilized state; it remains that this expense must, the greater part of it, be defrayed by taxes of one kind or another; the people contributing a part of their own private revenue, in order to make up a public revenue to the sovereign or commonwealth.
p22.zh: 因此,公有财产和公共土地这两个收入来源可能特别属于主权或联邦,是支付任何伟大和文明国家必要开支的不适当和不足的资金;这一开支的大部分必须用这种或那种税收来支付;人民将自己的私人收入的一部分贡献给主权或联邦,以弥补公共收入。

p24.original: The private revenue of individuals, it has been shown in the first book of this Inquiry, arises, ultimately from three different sources; rent, profit, and wages. Every tax must finally be paid from some one or other of those three different sources of revenue, or from all of them indifferently. I shall endeavour to give the best account I can, first, of those taxes which, it is intended should fall upon rent; secondly, of those which, it is intended should fall upon profit; thirdly, of those which, it is intended should fall upon wages; and fourthly, of those which, it is intended should fall indifferently upon all those three different sources of private revenue. The particular consideration of each of these four different sorts of taxes will divide the second part of the present chapter into four articles, three of which will require several other subdivisions. Many of these taxes, it will appear from the following review, are not finally paid from the fund, or source of revenue, upon which it is intended they should fall.
p24.zh: 个人的私人收入,在本调查的第一册中已经显示,最终来自三个不同来源:租金、利润和工资。每一税项最终都必须从这三种不同收入来源中的一种或另一种来源支付,或者从所有这些来源中无动于衷地支付。 我将努力尽力说明,首先,这些税项的用意应该是租金;其次,这些税项的用意应该是利润;其三,这些税项的用意应该是工资;其四,这些税项的用意应该是无动于衷地落在所有三种不同的私人收入来源上。 对这四种不同税种中的每一种进行特别的考虑,将本章第二部分分为四条,其中三条需要另外几个分支. 这些税项中的许多,从下文的审查来看,最终不是从基金或收入来源中支付,它们本来应该依靠该基金或收入来源。

p25.original: Before I enter upon the examination of particular taxes, it is necessary to premise the four following maximis with regard to taxes in general.
p25.zh: 在我开始审查特定税种之前,有必要就一般税种假定以下四个最大值。

p26.original: 1. The subjects of every state ought to contribute towards the support of the government, as nearly as possible, in proportion to their respective abilities; that is, in proportion to the revenue which they respectively enjoy under the protection of the state. The expense of government to the individuals of a great nation, is like the expense of management to the joint tenants of a great estate, who are all obliged to contribute in proportion to their respective interests in the estate. In the observation or neglect of this maxim, consists what is called the equality or inequality of taxation. Every tax, it must be observed once for all, which falls finally upon one only of the three sorts of revenue above mentioned, is necessarily unequal, in so far as it does not affect the other two. In the following examination of different taxes, I shall seldom take much farther notice of this sort of inequality; but shall, in most cases, confine my observations to that inequality which is occasioned by a particular tax falling unequally upon that particular sort of private revenue which is affected by it.
p26.zh: 1. 国家各州的主体应当根据各自的能力,即各自在国家保护下享有的收入的比例,尽可能为政府的支持作出贡献。 政府给一个伟大国家的个人的费用,就像管理一个伟大庄园的共同租户的费用,他们都有义务按照各自在庄园中的利益按比例缴款. 在观察或忽视这一准则时,包括所谓的税收平等或不平等。每项税收必须一劳永逸地遵守,而最后只属于上述三种收入中的一种,必然是不平等的,因为它不影响另外两种。 在对不同的税收进行下面的审查时,我很少更深入地注意到这种不平等;但在多数情况下,我的看法将限于一种不平等,这种不平等是由一种税收不平等地流向受到这种税收影响的某种私人收入造成的。

p27.original: 2. The tax which each individual is bound to pay, ought to be certain and not arbitrary. The time of payment, the manner of payment, the quantity to be paid, ought all to be clear and plain to the contributor, and to every other person. Where it is otherwise, every person subject to the tax is put more or less in the power of the tax-gatherer, who can either aggravate the tax upon any obnoxious contributor, or extort, by the terror of such aggravation, some present or perquisite to himself. The uncertainty of taxation encourages the insolence, and favours the corruption, of an order of men who are naturally unpopular, even where they are neither insolent nor corrupt. The certainty of what each individual ought to pay is, in taxation, a matter of so great importance, that a very considerable degree of inequality, it appears, I believe, from the experience of all nations, is not near so great an evil as a very small degree of uncertainty.
p27.zh: 2. 国家每个人必须缴纳的税款应该是确定的,而不是任意的。付款时间、付款方式、付款数量都应当清楚清楚,对缴款人和所有其他人来说都是明晰的。 在其他情况下,每个应纳税的人都或多或少地被征收税款者所支配,他们既可以加重任何恶毒的缴款者的税收,也可以通过这种加重的恐怖来勒索自己,有些是现身的,或是完全自以为是的。税收的不确定性鼓励了自然不受欢迎的人的暴虐和腐败,即使他们既不傲慢也不腐败。 在税收方面,每个人应该支付的费用的确定性非常重要,因此,我认为,从所有国家的经验来看,相当程度的不平等并不是一个非常严重的罪恶,而是一个极小的不确定性。

p28.original: 3. Every tax ought to be levied at the time, or in the manner, in which it is most likely to be convenient for the contributor to pay it. A tax upon the rent of land or of houses, payable at the same term at which such rents are usually paid, is levied at the time when it is most likely to be convenient for the contributor to pay; or when he is most likely to have wherewithall to pay. Taxes upon such consumable goods as are articles of luxury, are all finally paid by the consumer, and generally in a manner that is very convenient for him. He pays them by little and little, as he has occasion to buy the goods. As he is at liberty too, either to buy or not to buy, as he pleases, it must be his own fault if he ever suffers any considerable inconveniency from such taxes.
p28.zh: 3个每一税项均应在当时或以缴款国最方便缴纳的方式征收。 对土地或房屋租金的征税,按通常支付这种租金的同一期限支付,在出资人最可能方便支付时征收;或者在他最有可能支付时征收。奢侈品等消费品的税收最终全部由消费者支付,一般以他非常方便的方式支付. 他付他们很少,因为他有机会购买这些货物。 由于他也享有自由,无论是买还是不买,只要他因这种税收而蒙受任何相当大的不便,这一定是他自己的过错。

p29.original: 4. Every tax ought to be so contrived, as both to take out and to keep out of the pockets of the people as little as possible, over and above what it brings into the public treasury of the state. A tax may either take out or keep out of the pockets of the people a great deal more than it brings into the public treasury, in the four following ways. First, the levying of it may require a great number of officers, whose salaries may eat up the greater part of the produce of the tax, and whose perquisites may impose another additional tax upon the people. Secondly, it may obstruct the industry of the people, and discourage them from applying to certain branches of business which might give maintenance and employment to great multitudes. While it obliges the people to pay, it may thus diminish, or perhaps destroy, some of the funds which might enable them more easily to do so. Thirdly, by the forfeitures and other penalties which those unfortunate individuals incur, who attempt unsuccessfully to evade the tax, it may frequently ruin them, and thereby put an end to the benefit which the community might have received from the employment of their capitals. An injudicious tax offers a great temptation to smuggling. But the penalties of smuggling must arise in proportion to the temptation. The law, contrary to all the ordinary principles of justice, first creates the temptation, and then punishes those who yield to it; and it commonly enhances the punishment, too, in proportion to the very circumstance which ought certainly to alleviate it, the temptation to commit the crime. {See Sketches of the History of Man page 474, and Seq.} Fourthly, by subjecting the people to the frequent visits and the odious examination of the tax-gatherers, it may expose them to much unnecessary trouble, vexation, and oppression; and though vexation is not, strictly speaking, expense, it is certainly equivalent to the expense at which every man would be willing to redeem himself from it. It is in some one or other of these four different ways, that taxes are frequently so much more burdensome to the people than they are beneficial to the sovereign.
p29.zh: 4 , 4 , 4 , 4 , 4 , 4 , 4 , 4每一税项都应该如此精心策划,既要取出,又要尽可能少地从人民的口袋中抽出,超越它给国库带来的东西.税收可能从人民口袋中抽出或从中抽出比它给国库带来的更多,有以下四种方式. 一,征收征收可能需要大量军官,其工资可能消耗了大部分的税收产品,其特权可能给人民另外加征额外的税收. 第二,它可能阻碍人民的工业,并阻止他们向某些可能为广大人民提供维持和就业的工商部门提出申请。 虽然它要求人民支付,但它可能因此减少或可能摧毁一些可能使他们更容易支付的资金。 第三,由于这些不幸的个人试图逃避税收但未成功而遭到没收和其他惩罚,这往往会破坏他们的利益,从而结束社区从其首都就业可能得到的利益。恶性税为走私提供了极大的诱惑。 但是,对走私的处罚必须与诱惑相称。法律违背所有普通的正义原则,首先制造诱惑,然后惩罚屈服者;它通常也根据理应减轻这种诱惑的情节,加强惩罚。 {见《人类历史》第474页和Seq。 }第四,通过频繁访问和对税收征收者进行令人憎恶的审查,它可能使他们面临许多不必要的麻烦、烦恼和压迫;虽然严格地说,它不是费用,但它当然相当于每个人愿意从它中赎回自己的费用。税收往往比对主权人有利更重,这四种不同方式中的一种或另一种方式是,对人民来说,税收往往比对主权人有利得多。

p30.original: The evident justice and utility of the foregoing maxims have recommended them, more or less, to the attention of all nations. All nations have endeavoured, to the best of their judgment, to render their taxes as equal as they could contrive; as certain, as convenient to the contributor, both the time and the mode of payment, and in proportion to the revenue which they brought to the prince, as little burdensome to the people. The following short review of some of the principal taxes which have taken place in different ages and countries, will show, that the endeavours of all nations have not in this respect been equally successful.
p30.zh: 上述准则显然具有正义性和效用,这或多或少是提请所有国家注意的。所有国家尽其所能,努力使其税收尽可能平等;当然,对缴款国来说,时间和支付方式都十分方便,而且与它们给王子带来的收入成比例,因为给人民带来的负担不大。 下面对不同时代和不同国家的一些主要税种进行的简短审查将表明,并非所有国家都在这方面的努力都取得了同样的成功。

p31.original: ARTICLE I.--Taxes upon Rent--Taxes upon the Rent of Land.
p31.zh: 第一条 土地租借税

p32.original: A tax upon the rent of land may either be imposed according to a certain canon, every district being valued at a curtain rent, which valuation is not afterwards to be altered; or it may be imposed in such a manner, as to vary with every variation in the real rent of the land, and to rise or fall with the improvement or declension of its cultivation.
p32.zh: 土地租金税可以按照一定的禅宗征收,每个区按幕租计价,事后不改变估价;也可以按照土地实际租金的千差万别征收,随着土地种植的改善或减少而增减.

p33.original: A land tax which, like that of Great Britain, is assessed upon each district according to a certain invariable canon, though it should be equal at the time of its first establishment, necessarily becomes unequal in process of time, according to the unequal degrees of improvement or neglect in the cultivation of the different parts of the country. In England, the valuation, according to which the different counties and parishes were assessed to the land tax by the 4th of William and Mary, was very unequal even at its first establishment. This tax, therefore, so far offends against the first of the four maxims above mentioned. It is perfectly agreeable to the other three. It is perfectly certain. The time of payment for the tax, being the same as that for the rent, is as convenient as it can be to the contributor. Though the landlord is, in all cases, the real contributor, the tax is commonly advanced by the tenant, to whom the landlord is obliged to allow it in the payment of the rent. This tax is levied by a much smaller number of officers than any other which affords nearly the same revenue. As the tax upon each district does not rise with the rise of the rent, the sovereign does not share in the profits of the landlord's improvements. Those improvements sometimes contribute, indeed, to the discharge of the other landlords of the district. But the aggravation of the tax, which this may sometimes occasion upon a particular estate, is always so very small, that it never can discourage those improvements, nor keep down the produce of the land below what it would otherwise rise to. As it has no tendency to diminish the quantity, it can have none to raise the price of that produce. It does not obstruct the industry of the people; it subjects the landlord to no other inconveniency besides the unavoidable one of paying the tax. The advantage, however, which the land-lord has derived from the invariable constancy of the valuation, by which all the lands of Great Britain are rated to the land-tax, has been principally owing to some circumstances altogether extraneous to the nature of the tax.
p33.zh: 土地税同大不列颠一样,按照某一不可变的国杖对每个区进行征税,尽管在第一次建立时应平等,但由于该国不同地区的种植改善或忽视程度不平等,在时间进程中必然变得不平等。 在英国,不同的郡和教区被威廉四世和玛丽评定为土地税的估值,即使在第一次建立时也非常不平等. 因此,这项税迄今违反了上述四项准则中的第一项。 这完全可以接受其他三个方面。绝对是肯定的。交税时间,与交租时间相同,对交税人来说,是同样方便的. 虽然房东在所有情况下都是真正的出资人,但通常由房客预付税款,房东有义务允许房东支付租金。 这种税收由比任何其他提供几乎相同收入的官员少得多的官员征收。 由于每个区的税额不会随着租金的上涨而增加,因此君主不分享地主改良的利润. 这些改善有时确实有助于该区其他房东的退房。 但是,税收的恶化有时可能发生在某一特定的庄园上,但这种恶化总是非常小,因此它永远不能阻止这些改善,也不能使土地的产量低于它本来能够达到的水平。 由于它没有减少数量的趋势,因此它没有办法提高这种产品的价格。 它不会阻碍人民的产业;除了不可避免的缴纳税款之外,它不会使房东受到其他不便。 然而,地主从估价的不可改变的不稳性中获得的优势是,大不列颠的所有土地都被评为土地税,这主要是由于某些情况与税种性质完全无关。

p34.original: It has been owing in part, to the great prosperity of almost every part of the country, the rents of almost all the estates of Great Britain having, since the time when this valuation was first established, been continually rising, and scarce any of them having fallen. The landlords, therefore, have almost all gained the difference between the tax which they would have paid, according to the present rent of their estates, and that which they actually pay according to the ancient valuation. Had the state of the country been different, had rents been gradually falling in consequence of the declension of cultivation, the landlords would almost all have lost this difference. In the state of things which has happened to take place since the revolution, the constancy of the valuation has been advantageous to the landlord and hurtful to the sovereign. In a different state of things it might have been advantageous to the sovereign and hurtful to the landlord.
p34.zh: 这部分是由于几乎全国每一个地区的繁荣,自第一次确定这种估价以来,英国几乎所有庄园的租金都在不断上涨,而且很少有人跌落。 因此,房东们几乎都获得了他们本该缴纳的税费,按照他们庄园目前的租金,和他们实际按照古代估价支付的税费之间的差额. 如果该国情况不同,如果由于种植面积的减少而逐渐减少,那么几乎所有的地主都会失去这种差别。 在自革命以来发生的事态中,估价的坚韧性对房东有利,对君主不利. 在不同的状态下,它可能对君主有利,对房东不利。

p35.original: As the tax is made payable in money, so the valuation of the land is expressed in money. Since the establishment of this valuation, the value of silver has been pretty uniform, and there has been no alteration in the standard of the coin, either as to weight or fineness. Had silver risen considerably in its value, as it seems to have done in the course of the two centuries which preceded the discovery of the mines of America, the constancy of the valuation might have proved very oppressive to the landlord. Had silver fallen considerably in its value, as it certainly did for about a century at least after the discovery of those mines, the same constancy of valuation would have reduced very much this branch of the revenue of the sovereign. Had any considerable alteration been made in the standard of the money, either by sinking the same quantity of silver to a lower denomination, or by raising it to a higher; had an ounce of silver, for example, instead of being coined into five shillings and two pence, been coined either into pieces which bore so low a denomination as two shillings and seven pence, or into pieces which bore so high a one as ten shillings and four pence, it would, in the one case, have hurt the revenue of the proprietor, in the other that of the sovereign.
p35.zh: 由于应纳税款是用金钱支付的,所以土地的估价是以金钱表示的.此次估值成立后,银币价值相当一致,硬币标准没有改变,无论是重量还是精细程度. 如果白银的价值大幅上升,正如在发现美国矿山之前的两个世纪中,白银的价值似乎已经大幅上升,那么,对地主的估价的坚持性可能证明是非常压迫性的。 如果银子的价值大幅下降,至少是在发现这些矿山后大约一个世纪的时间里,那么同样的估价方式会大大降低主权收入的这一分支。 如果货币标准有任何重大改变,要么将同样数量的银子下沉到较低的面额,要么将其提升到更高的面额;例如,一盎司的银子不是被铸成5先令和2便士,而是被铸成面额如此低的2先令和7便士的硬币,或者被铸成10先令和4便士的硬币,在一种情况下会损害业主的收入,在另一种情况下,会损害主权人的收入。

p36.original: In circumstances, therefore, somewhat different from those which have actually taken place, this constancy of valuation might have been a very great inconveniency, either to the contributors or to the commonwealth. In the course of ages, such circumstances, however, must at some time or other happen. But though empires, like all the other works of men, have all hitherto proved mortal, yet every empire aims at immortality. Every constitution, therefore, which it is meant should be as permanent as the empire itself, ought to be convenient, not in certain circumstances only, but in all circumstances; or ought to be suited, not to those circumstances which are transitory, occasional, or accidental, but to those which are necessary, and therefore always the same.
p36.zh: 因此,在与实际发生的情况有些不同的情况下,这种不稳的估价可能对于捐助者或联邦来说是非常不方便的。 然而,在年龄过程中,这种情况必须发生在某个时候或其他时候。 但是,虽然帝国,像人类的所有其他作品一样, 已经证明所有的人, 然而每一个帝国都以不朽为目的。 因此,每一部宪法,其本意应与帝国本身一样永久,应该方便,不仅在某些情况下,而且在所有情况下;或者应该适合,而不是那些过渡性、偶然性或偶然性的情况,而是那些必要的情况,因此永远是相同的。

p37.original: A tax upon the rent of land, which varies with every variation of the rent, or which rises and falls according to the improvement or neglect of cultivation, is recommended by that sect of men of letters in France, who call themselves the economists, as the most equitable of all taxes. All taxes, they pretend, fall ultimately upon the rent of land, and ought, therefore, to be imposed equally upon the fund which must finally pay them. That all taxes ought to fall as equally as possible upon the fund which must finally pay them, is certainly true. But without entering into the disagreeable discussion of the metaphysical arguments by which they support their very ingenious theory, it will sufficiently appear, from the following review, what are the taxes which fall finally upon the rent of the land, and what are those which fall finally upon some other fund.
p37.zh: 土地租金税因租金的每一种变化而异,或因种植的改善或忽视而增减,法国的这一信使自称经济学家的那一派建议作为所有税中最公平的税. 他们假装,所有税项最终都落在土地的租金上,因此,应该平等地强加给最终必须支付这些税项的基金。 所有税项都应该尽可能平等地落在必须最终支付税项的基金身上,这无疑是事实。 但是,如果不对支持他们非常有才智的理论的元物理论点进行不满意的讨论,那么从下面的审查中就足以看出,最终落在土地租金上的税项是什么,最后落在其他一些基金上的税项是什么。

p38.original: In the Venetian territory, all the arable lands which are given in lease to farmers are taxed at a tenth of the rent. {Memoires concernant les Droits, p. 240, 241.} The leases are recorded in a public register, which is kept by the officers of revenue in each province or district. When the proprietor cultivates his own lands, they are valued according to an equitable estimation, and he is allowed a deduction of one-fifth of the tax; so that for such land he pays only eight instead of ten per cent. of the supposed rent.
p38.zh: 在威尼斯地区,所有出租给农民的耕地均按租金的十分之一征税。240, 241.} 租约在公共登记簿中登记,由各省或区税务官员保管。 当土地所有者耕种自己的土地时,按照公平的估计估价土地,并允许他扣除五分之一的税款;因此,对于这种土地,他只支付假定租金的八分之十。

p39.original: A land-tax of this kind is certainly more equal than the land-tax of England. It might not, perhaps, be altogether so certain, and the assessment of the tax might frequently occasion a good deal more trouble to the landlord. It might, too, be a good deal more expensive in the levying.
p39.zh: 这种土地税当然比英格兰的土地税更平等. 也许它并不完全如此确定,对税收的评估往往给房东带来更多的麻烦。征收税费可能也比这贵得多。

p40.original: Such a system of administration, however, might, perhaps, be contrived, as would in a great measure both prevent this uncertainty, and moderate this expense.
p40.zh: 然而,这种管理制度或许可以设计,因为在很大程度上既可以防止这种不确定性,又可以减少这种开支。

p41.original: The landlord and tenant, for example, might jointly be obliged to record their lease in a public register. Proper penalties might be enacted against concealing or misrepresenting any of the conditions; and if part of those penalties were to be paid to either of the two parties who informed against and convicted the other of such concealment or misrepresentation, it would effectually deter them from combining together in order to defraud the public revenue. All the conditions of the lease might be sufficiently known from such a record.
p41.zh: 例如,房东和房客可能共同有义务在公共登记册中登记其租约。可对隐瞒或谎报任何条件的行为处以适当惩罚;如果将部分惩罚支付给对另一方进行隐瞒或谎报并定罪的任何一方,则实际上会阻止他们为了骗取公共收入而合并在一起。 从这种记录中可能充分了解租赁的所有条件。

p42.original: Some landlords, instead of raising the rent, take a fine for the renewal of the lease. This practice is, in most cases, the expedient of a spendthrift, who, for a sum of ready money sells a future revenue of much greater value. It is, in most cases, therefore, hurtful to the landlord; it is frequently hurtful to the tenant; and it is always hurtful to the community. It frequently takes from the tenant so great a part of his capital, and thereby diminishes so much his ability to cultivate the land, that he finds it more difficult to pay a small rent than it would otherwise have been to pay a great one. Whatever diminishes his ability to cultivate, necessarily keeps down, below what it would otherwise have been, the most important part of the revenue of the community. By rendering the tax upon such fines a good deal heavier than upon the ordinary rent, this hurtful practice might be discouraged, to the no small advantage of all the different parties concerned, of the landlord, of the tenant, of the sovereign, and of the whole community.
p42.zh: 部分房东没有提高租金,而是对续租收取罚款.在大多数情况下,这种做法是花钱者的权宜之计,就一笔现成的钱而言,他出售的将来收入的价值要高得多。 因此,在大多数情况下,它伤害房东;它常常伤害房客;它总是伤害社区。租户常常要他资本的很大一部分,从而削弱了他耕种土地的能力,以致他发现支付小额租金比支付巨额租金更为困难。 无论什么削弱了他的种植能力,都必然会降低到本来会是社区收入中最重要的部分的水平。 如果使这种罚款的征税比普通租金重,这种有害的做法可能会受到劝阻,使所有有关当事方、房东、房客、主权者和整个社区都受益匪浅。

p43.original: Some leases prescribe to the tenant a certain mode of cultivation, and a certain succession of crops, during the whole continuance of the lease. This condition, which is generally the effect of the landlord's conceit of his own superior knowledge (a conceit in most cases very ill-founded), ought always to be considered as an additional rent, as a rent in service, instead of a rent in money. In order to discourage the practice, which is generally a foolish one, this species of rent might be valued rather high, and consequently taxed somewhat higher than common money-rents.
p43.zh: 有些租约规定租户在整个租约续期期间有某种耕作方式和某种作物的继承。 这一条件,一般是房东自以为是(在大多数情况下,这种自以为是是是完全没有根据的)的结果,应始终视为额外租金,作为服务租金,而不是金钱租金。 为了劝阻这种做法,这种租金的价值可能相当高,因此比普通的租金要高一些。

p44.original: Some landlords, instead of a rent in money, require a rent in kind, in corn, cattle, poultry, wine, oil, etc.; others, again, require a rent in service. Such rents are always more hurtful to the tenant than beneficial to the landlord. They either take more, or keep more out of the pocket of the former, than they put into that of the latter. In every country where they take place, the tenants are poor and beggarly, pretty much according to the degree in which they take place. By valuing, in the same manner, such rents rather high, and consequently taxing them somewhat higher than common money-rents, a practice which is hurtful to the whole community, might, perhaps, be sufficiently discouraged.
p44.zh: 有些房东不收钱租,而是要求以实物,玉米,牛,家禽,葡萄酒,油料等为单位的租金;另一些房东又要求按期租房. 这种租金对房客的伤害往往大于对房东的伤害。 他们要么多拿,要么少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少,或用少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少,或用少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少放少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少拿少, 在每一个发生这种情况的国家里,租户都是穷人和乞丐,几乎是根据其发生的程度而定的。 同样,通过估价这种租金相当高,并因此对租金征收比普通租金高一些的税,这种做法对整个社会都有害,也许足以劝阻他们。

p45.original: When the landlord chose to occupy himself a part of his own lands, the rent might be valued according to an equitable arbitration of the farmers and landlords in the neighbourhood, and a moderate abatement of the tax might be granted to him, in the same manner as in the Venetian territory, provided the rent of the lands which he occupied did not exceed a certain sum. It is of importance that the landlord should be encouraged to cultivate a part of his own land. His capital is generally greater than that of the tenant, and, with less skill, he can frequently raise a greater produce. The landlord can afford to try experiments, and is generally disposed to do so. His unsuccessful experiments occasion only a moderate loss to himself. His successful ones contribute to the improvement and better cultivation of the whole country. It might be of importance, however, that the abatement of the tax should encourage him to cultivate to a certain extent only. If the landlords should, the greater part of them, be tempted to farm the whole of their own lands, the country (instead of sober and industrious tenants, who are bound by their own interest to cultivate as well as their capital and skill will allow them) would be filled with idle and profligate bailiffs, whose abusive management would soon degrade the cultivation, and reduce the annual produce of the land, to the diminution, not only of the revenue of their masters, but of the most important part of that of the whole society.
p45.zh: 当地主选择占有自己部分土地时,租金可能根据附近农民和地主的公平仲裁来估价,并且可以象在威尼斯地区那样,以适度减税的方式给予他,只要他所占用土地的租金不超过一定数额。 重要的是,应鼓励地主耕种他自己的部分土地。 他的资本一般都大于租户的资本,由于技术水平较低,他可以经常筹集更大的产品.地主可以负担尝试实验的费用,一般都愿意这样做. 他的实验失败,只给自己造成了中度损失. 他的成功者为全国的改善和更好的种植作出了贡献。 然而,减少税收可能只应鼓励他在某种程度上种植。 如果地主(他们中的大部分人)被诱惑耕种他们自己的全部土地,国家(而不是清醒和勤奋的租户,他们受自身利益的约束,从事耕种以及他们的资本和技能将允许他们)将充满闲置和挥霍的法警,他们的滥权管理将很快降低耕种,并减少土地的年产量,不仅减少他们主人的收入,而且减少整个社会最重要的部分的收入。

p46.original: Such a system of administration might, perhaps, free a tax of this kind from any degree of uncertainty, which could occasion either oppression or inconveniency to the contributor; and might, at the same time, serve to introduce into the common management of land such a plan of policy as might contribute a good deal to the general improvement and good cultivation of the country.
p46.zh: 这种管理制度也许可以使这种税从任何程度的不确定性中解脱出来,这种不确定性可能给出资者造成压迫或不便;同时,这种管理制度还可能有助于在土地的共同管理中引入一种政策计划,从而对总体改善和良好耕作作出很大贡献。

p47.original: The expense of levying a land-tax, which varied with every variation of the rent, would, no doubt, be somewhat greater than that of levying one which was always rated according to a fixed valuation. Some additional expense would necessarily be incurred, both by the different register-offices which it would be proper to establish in the different districts of the country, and by the different valuations which might occasionally be made of the lands which the proprietor chose to occupy himself. The expense of all this, however, might be very moderate, and much below what is incurred in the levying of many other taxes, which afford a very inconsiderable revenue in comparison of what might easily be drawn from a tax of this kind.
p47.zh: 征收土地税的费用随着租金的变动而不同,这无疑会比征收土地税的费用多一些,而征收土地税总是按照固定的估价来评定。必然要增加一些费用,无论是在该国不同地区适当设立的不同的登记办事处,还是偶尔对业主选择占有的土地作不同的估价。 然而,所有这些开支可能非常小,远远低于征收许多其他税收的费用,这些税收与从这类税收中轻松获得的收入相比,收入非常少。

p48.original: The discouragement which a variable land-tax of this kind might give to the improvement of land, seems to be the most important objection which can be made to it. The landlord would certainly be less disposed to improve, when the sovereign, who contributed nothing to the expense, was to share in the profit of the improvement. Even this objection might, perhaps, be obviated, by allowing the landlord, before he began his improvement, to ascertain, in conjunction with the officers of revenue, the actual value of his lands, according to the equitable arbitration of a certain number of landlords and farmers in the neighbourhood, equally chosen by both parties: and by rating him, according to this valuation, for such a number of years as might be fully sufficient for his complete indemnification. To draw the attention of the sovereign towards the improvement of the land, from a regard to the increase of his own revenue, is one or the principal advantages proposed by this species of land-tax. The term, therefore, allowed, for the indemnification of the landlord, ought not to be a great deal longer than what was necessary for that purpose, lest the remoteness of the interest should discourage too much this attention. It had better, however, be somewhat too long, than in any respect too short. No incitement to the attention of the sovereign can ever counterbalance the smallest discouragement to that of the landlord. The attention of the sovereign can be, at best, but a very general and vague consideration of what is likely to contribute to the better cultivation of the greater part of his dominions. The attention of the landlord is a particular and minute consideration of what is likely to be the most advantageous application of every inch of ground upon his estate. The principal attention of the sovereign ought to be, to encourage, by every means in his power, the attention both of the landlord and of the farmer, by allowing both to pursue their own interest in their own way, and according to their own judgment; by giving to both the most perfect security that they shall enjoy the full recompence of their own industry; and by procuring to both the most extensive market for every part of their produce, in consequence of establishing the easiest and safest communications, both by land and by water, through every part of his own dominions, as well as the most unbounded freedom of exportation to the dominions of all other princes.
p48.zh: 这种可变的土地税可能对土地的改善产生抑制作用,似乎是可以对此提出的最重要反对。地主当然不会愿意改善,因为主权者不为这笔费用作任何贡献,而是分享改善的利润。即使是这种异议,也许也可以排除,在房东开始改善之前,允许他与收入官一起,根据双方平等选择的邻里一定数量的房东和农民的公平仲裁,确定他的土地的实际价值;并根据这一估价,将他评为足以使他得到完全赔偿的几年。吸引主权者注意改善土地,从增加自己的收入的角度出发,是这种土地税的一种或主要好处。 因此,为了补偿房东,这一用语不应比为此目的所必要的时间长很多,以免利息的偏僻性会阻止人们过多地注意这个问题。 然而,这总比任何方面都短长一些好。任何煽动主权者注意的行为都无法抵消地主的最小的不满。君主的注意力充其量只能是对于什么可能有助于更好地种植他的大部分领地的非常笼统和模糊的考虑。房东的注意是特别的,而且只是一时的考虑,考虑什么可能是对其财产每一寸土地的最有利适用。主权者的主要注意力应该是,通过他力所能及的一切手段,鼓励地主和农民的注意,允许他们以自己的方式和根据自己的判断追求自己的利益;给予他们最完美的安全,使他们享有自己工业的充分恢复;以及为其每一部分产品采购最广泛的市场,通过他自己的领地的每一个部分,通过土地和水路,建立最容易和安全的通讯,以及最不受限制地向所有其他王子的领地出口的自由。

p49.original: If, by such a system of administration, a tax of this kind could be so managed as to give, not only no discouragement, but, on the contrary, some encouragement to the improvement or land, it does not appear likely to occasion any other inconveniency to the landlord, except always the unavoidable one of being obliged to pay the tax. In all the variations of the state of the society, in the improvement and in the declension of agriculture; in all the variations in the value of silver, and in all those in the standard of the coin, a tax of this kind would, of its own accord, and without any attention of government, readily suit itself to the actual situation of things, and would be equally just and equitable in all those different changes. It would, therefore, be much more proper to be established as a perpetual and unalterable regulation, or as what is called a fundamental law of the commonwealth, than any tax which was always to be levied according to a certain valuation.
p49.zh: 如果通过这种管理制度,这种税收的管理能够做到不仅不令人沮丧,而且相反地鼓励改良或土地,那么它似乎不会给房东带来任何其他不便,除非总是不可避免的必须缴纳税款。 在社会状况的各种变异中,在农业的改善和减产方面;在银币价值的各种变异中,在硬币标准上的所有变异中,这种税会自发地,在政府不注意的情况下,很容易地适应事物的实际情况,并且在所有这些不同变化中,都是同样公正和公平的. 因此,比起任何根据某种估价总是征收的税项,更应该确立为永久的、不可改变的条例,或被称为联邦基本法的条例。

p50.original: Some states, instead of the simple and obvious expedient of a register of leases, have had recourse to the laborious and expensive one of an actual survey and valuation of all the lands in the country. They have suspected, probably, that the lessor and lessee, in order to defraud the public revenue, might combine to conceal the real terms of the lease. Doomsday-book seems to have been the result of a very accurate survey of this kind.
p50.zh: 一些州没有象租赁登记那样简单和明显地方便,而是求助于对国内所有土地进行实际调查和估价的费力和昂贵的一次。 他们怀疑,也许出租人和承租人为了骗取公共收入,可能合在一起掩盖租赁的实际条件。最终日记似乎是这种非常精确的调查的结果。

p51.original: In the ancient dominions of the king of Prussia, the land-tax is assessed according to an actual survey and valuation, which is reviewed and altered from time to time. {Memoires concurent les Droits, etc. tom, i. p. 114, 115, 116, etc.} According to that valuation, the lay proprietors pay from twenty to twenty-five per cent. of their revenue; ecclesiastics from forty to forty-five per cent. The survey and valuation of Silesia was made by order of the present king, it is said, with great accuracy. According to that valuation, the lands belonging to the bishop of Breslaw are taxed at twenty-five per cent. of their rent. The other revenues of the ecclesiastics of both religions at fifty per cent. The commanderies of the Teutonic order, and of that of Malta, at forty per cent. Lands held by a noble tenure, at thirty-eight and one-third per cent. Lands held by a base tenure, at thirty-five and one-third per cent.
p51.zh: 在普鲁士国王的古代统治中,土地税根据实际的调查和估价来评估,这种调查和估价不时地加以审查和修改。114, 115, 116等) 根据该估价,非专业业主支付其收入的25%至25%;教会费从40%至45%。 据说,西里西亚的勘测和估价是按现任国王的命令进行的,非常准确。 根据该估价,属于布雷斯瓦夫主教的土地按其租金的25%征税.两种宗教教会的其他收入为50%。Teutonic命令的指挥官和马耳他命令的指挥官占40%。贵族保有权占有的土地占38%和三分之一。拥有基本保有权的土地占35%和三分之一。

p52.original: The survey and valuation of Bohemia is said to have been the work of more than a hundred years. It was not perfected till after the peace of 1748, by the orders of the present empress queen. {Id. tom i. p.85, 84.} The survey of the duchy of Milan, which was begun in the time of Charles VI., was not perfected till after 1760 It is esteemed one of the most accurate that has ever been made. The survey of Savoy and Piedmont was executed under the orders of the late king of Sardinia. {Id. p. 280, etc.; also p, 287. etc. to 316.}
p52.zh: 据说,对波希米亚的调查和估价是一百多年的工作. 直到1748年和平之后,才被现在的女王下令完善. {Id. Tom i. p. 85, 84.} 开始于查理六世时期的米兰公爵领地调查直到1760年以后才完善. . 对萨伏依和皮埃蒙特的调查是在撒丁岛已故国王的命令下执行的. {Id. p.280, et .; 也第287页等至316.}

p53.original: In the dominions of the king of Prussia, the revenue of the church is taxed much higher than that of lay proprietors. The revenue of the church is, the greater part of it, a burden upon the rent of land. It seldom happens that any part of it is applied towards the improvement of land; or is so employed as to contribute, in any respect, towards increasing the revenue of the great body of the people. His Prussian majesty had probably, upon that account, thought it reasonable that it should contribute a good deal more towards relieving the exigencies of the state. In some countries, the lands of the church are exempted from all taxes. In others, they are taxed more lightly than other lands. In the duchy of Milan, the lands which the church possessed before 1575, are rated to the tax at a third only or their value.
p53.zh: 在普鲁士国王的统治下,教会的收入比非宗教业主的税收要高得多.教堂的收入,其更大的部分,是土地租金的负担.很少发生以下情况:一部分土地用于改善土地;或者用于在任何方面为增加人民大军的收入作出贡献。普鲁士陛下可能因此认为,应该为缓解国家的紧急局势作出更大的贡献,这是合理的。 在一些国家,教会的土地免征一切税. 在另一些国家,其征税比其他土地要轻。 在米兰的杜希,教会在1575年以前拥有的土地,被评为只有三分之一的税额或其价值.

p54.original: In Silesia, lands held by a noble tenure are taxed three per cent. higher than those held by a base tenure. The honours and privileges of different kinds annexed to the former, his Prussian majesty had probably imagined, would sufficiently compensate to the proprietor a small aggravation of the tax; while, at the same time, the humiliating inferiority of the latter would be in some measure alleviated, by being taxed somewhat more lightly. In other countries, the system of taxation, instead of alleviating, aggravates this inequality. In the dominions of the king of Sardinia, and in those provinces of France which are subject to what is called the real or predial taille, the tax falls altogether upon the lands held by a base tenure. Those held by a noble one are exempted.
p54.zh: 在西里西亚,贵族土地保有权拥有的土地被征税3%,高于基保有权拥有的土地. 他的普鲁士陛下可能想象到,前者所兼并的各类荣誉和特权将足以补偿业主略微加重的税收;同时,通过略为放松征税,后者的屈辱人格将在某种程度上得到减轻。 在其他国家,税收制度不是减轻,而是加剧了这种不平等。 在撒丁岛国王的领地中,以及在法国那些受所谓实际或先天尾巴制约的省份,税收完全落在基本土地保有权所持有的土地上。尊者所持者免.

p55.original: A land tax assessed according to a general survey and valuation, how equal soever it may be at first, must, in the course of a very moderate period of time, become unequal. To prevent its becoming so would require the continual and painful attention of government to all the variations in the state and produce of every different farm in the country. The governments of Prussia, of Bohemia, of Sardinia, and of the duchy of Milan, actually exert an attention of this kind; an attention so unsuitable to the nature of government, that it is not likely to be of long continuance, and which, if it is continued, will probably, in the long-run, occasion much more trouble and vexation than it can possibly bring relief to the contributors.
p55.zh: 根据一般调查和估价评估的土地税,无论一开始多么平等,在很短的时间内,都必须成为不平等的。为防止这种情况的出现,政府需要持续和痛苦地关注国家的各种变化以及国内每个不同农场的生产。普鲁士、波希米亚、撒丁岛和米兰的德共政府实际上都给予这种关注;对政府性质如此不适当的关注,以致不可能长期持续下去,如果继续下去,从长远来看,这很可能带来更多的麻烦和烦恼,甚至无法给贡献者带来救济。

p56.original: In 1666, the generality of Montauban was assessed to the real or predial taille, according, it is said, to a very exact survey and valuation. {Memoires concernant les Droits, etc. tom. ii p. 139, etc.} By 1727, this assessment had become altogether unequal. In order to remedy this inconveniency, government has found no better expedient, than to impose upon the whole generality an additional tax of a hundred and twenty thousand livres. This additional tax is rated upon all the different districts subject to the taille according to the old assessment. But it is levied only upon those which, in the actual state of things, are by that assessment under-taxed; and it is applied to the relief of those which, by the same assessment, are over-taxed. Two districts, for example, one of which ought, in the actual state of things, to be taxed at nine hundred, the other at eleven hundred livres, are, by the old assessment, both taxed at a thousand livres. Both these districts are, by the additional tax, rated at eleven hundred livres each. But this additional tax is levied only upon the district under-charged, and it is applied altogether to the relief of that overcharged, which consequently pays only nine hundred livres. The government neither gains nor loses by the additional tax, which is applied altogether to remedy the inequalities arising from the old assessment. The application is pretty much regulated according to the discretion of the intendant of the generality, and must, therefore, be in a great measure arbitrary.
p56.zh: 据说,1666年,根据非常精确的调查和估价,对Montauban的概况进行了实际或前尾部的评估。 到1727年,这一评估已完全不平等。 为了弥补这种不便,政府发现没有什么比对一般人再加征12万里弗尔的税收更方便了。 根据旧的评估,对受尾巴管制的所有不同区都征收这种附加税。 但只向那些在实际状况下因评估税额不足而征税的人征收;并且适用于对根据同样评估而征税过高的人的救济。 例如,两个区,一个在实际状况下应该征税九百,另一个在1100里弗,根据旧的评估,两个区都征税一千里弗。 这两个区按附加税额分别评为1100里弗。 但这种附加税只征收给征收不足的县,而完全适用于减免征收的超额税,因此只支付九百里弗。 政府不因增加的税收而增益,而增加的税收完全用来弥补旧的评估所产生的不平等。申请几乎是按笼统的意向来加以管制的,因此必须在很大程度上是任意的。

p57.original: Taxes which are proportioned, not in the Rent, but to the Produce of Land.
p57.zh: 税分分,不以租置,而以地产为主.

p58.original: Taxes upon the produce of land are, In reality, taxes upon the rent; and though they may be originally advanced by the farmer, are finally paid by the landlord. When a certain portion of the produce is to be paid away for a tax, the farmer computes as well as he can, what the value of this portion is, one year with another, likely to amount to, and he makes a proportionable abatement in the rent which he agrees to pay to the landlord. There is no farmer who does not compute beforehand what the church tythe, which is a land tax of this kind, is, one year with another, likely to amount to.
p58.zh: 实际上,对土地产地征税是租金税;虽然这些税项最初可能由农民垫付,但最终由地主支付。 当某一部分的农产品要付税时,农民会尽可能计算出这部分的价值,一年与另一年的价值,很可能达到,他还按比例减少他同意付给房东的租金。没有一个农民事先不计算教会税,即这种土地税,一年又一年,可能相当于什么。

p59.original: The tythe, and every other land tax of this kind, under the appearance of perfect equality, are very unequal taxes; a certain portion of the produce being in differrent situations, equivalent to a very different portion of the rent. In some very rich lands, the produce is so great, that the one half of it is fully sufficient to replace to the farmer his capital employed in cultivation, together with the ordinary profits of farming stock in the neighbourhood. The other half, or, what comes to the same thing, the value of the other half, he could afford to pay as rent to the landlord, if there was no tythe. But if a tenth of the produce is taken from him in the way of tythe, he must require an abatement of the fifth part of his rent, otherwise he cannot get back his capital with the ordinary profit. In this case, the rent of the landlord, instead of amounting to a half, or five-tenths of the whole produce, will amount only to four-tenths of it. In poorer lands, on the contrary, the produce is sometimes so small, and the expense of cultivation so great, that it requires four-fifths of the whole produce, to replace to the farmer his capital with the ordinary profit. In this case, though there was no tythe, the rent of the landlord could amount to no more than one-fifth or two-tenths of the whole produce. But if the farmer pays one-tenth of the produce in the way of tythe, he must require an equal abatement of the rent of the landlord, which will thus be reduced to one-tenth only of the whole produce. Upon the rent of rich lands the tythe may sometimes be a tax of no more than one-fifth part, or four shillings in the pound; whereas upon that of poorer lands, it may sometimes be a tax of one half, or of ten shillings in the pound.
p59.zh: 在表面上完全平等的情况下,这种土地税和所有其他土地税都是非常不平等的税;一部分的农产品情况不同,相当于租金的非常不同的一部分。在一些非常富饶的土地上,农产品非常丰盛,其中一半完全足以取代农民从事种植业的资本,加上附近农户的普通利润。 另一半,或者,什么来到同样的事情, 另一半的价值, 他可以支付作为租金 房东,如果没有tythe。 但是,如果以太宗之道从他手中抢走了十分之一的产物,他必须要求减掉他的第五部分租金,否则他就不能用普通利润收回他的资本. 在这种情况下,地主的租金,与其说相当于一半,或者说整个产物的五十分之一,只相当于四十分之一. 相反,在较贫瘠的土地上,生产有时如此之小,而种植的成本如此之大,需要占整个生产的五分之四,才能用普通利润来代替农民的资本. 在这种情况下,虽然没有大字报,但地主的租金可能不超过整个农产品的五分之一或十分之二。 但是,如果农户以太乙的方式支付十分之一的产物,他必须要求同等减轻地主的租金,这样,将减少到只有全部产物的十分之一.富人租地时,有时税额不超过五分之一,或4先令,以英镑计;而较贫穷的地上,有时税额可能为一半,或10先令。

p60.original: The tythe, as it is frequently a very unequal tax upon the rent, so it is always a great discouragement, both to the improvements of the landlord, and to the cultivation of the farmer. The one cannot venture to make the most important, which are generally the most expensive improvements; nor the other to raise the most valuable, which are generally, too, the most expensive crops; when the church, which lays out no part of the expense, is to share so very largely in the profit. The cultivation of madder was, for a long time, confined by the tythe to the United Provinces, which, being presbyterian countries, and upon that account exempted from this destructive tax, enjoyed a sort of monopoly of that useful dyeing drug against the rest of Europe. The late attempts to introduce the culture of this plant into England, have been made only in consequence of the statute, which enacted that five shillings an acre should be received in lieu of all manner of tythe upon madder.
p60.zh: ⁇ 者,因其往往对租界征收极不平等的税,所以无论对地主的改良,还是对农民的耕种,都始终是一个很大的劝阻.一方不能冒险制造最重要的,一般是最昂贵的改良;另一方则不能筹集最有价值的,一般也是最昂贵的作物;当教堂不花部分费用时,则要如此大份地分享利润.长久以来,疯狂的种植一直受到联合省份的束缚,这些省份是长老会国家,因此免征这种破坏性税,对欧洲其他地区的这种有用的染色药物享有某种垄断。晚期试图将这种植物的文化引入英国,只是因为该法规颁布,一亩五先令应代替疯狂的任何事情。

p61.original: As through the greater part of Europe, the church, so in many different countries of Asia, the state, is principally supported by a land tax, proportioned not to the rent, but to the produce of the land. In China, the principal revenue of the sovereign consists in a tenth part of the produce of all the lands of the empire. This tenth part, however, is estimated so very moderately, that, in many provinces, it is said not to exceed a thirtieth part of the ordinary produce. The land tax or land rent which used to be paid to the Mahometan government of Bengal, before that country fell into the hands of the English East India company, is said to have amounted to about a fifth part of the produce. The land tax of ancient Egypt is said likewise to have amounted to a fifth part.
p61.zh: 与欧洲大部分地区一样,该教堂,因此在亚洲许多不同国家,该州,主要靠土地税作为支撑,不按租金,而是按土地的产地来分配.在中国,君主的主要收入包括帝国所有土地的第十部分。 然而,这第十部分估计非常中度,以至于在许多省份,据说不超过普通产品中的第三十部分。 据说,在孟加拉马荷曼政府落入英属东印度公司手中之前,过去支付给该国政府的土地税或土地租金大约相当于该农产品的五分之一。 据说古埃及的土地税也相当于第五部分。

p62.original: In Asia, this sort of land tax is said to interest the sovereign in the improvement and cultivation of land. The sovereigns of China, those of Bengal while under the Mahometan govermnent, and those of ancient Egypt, are said, accordingly, to have been extremely attentive to the making and maintaining of good roads and navigable canals, in order to increase, as much as possible, both the quantity and value of every part of the produce of the land, by procuring to every part of it the most extensive market which their own dominions could afford. The tythe of the church is divided into such small portions that no one of its proprietors can have any interest of this kind. The parson of a parish could never find his account, in making a road or canal to a distant part of the country, in order to extend the market for the produce of his own particular parish. Such taxes, when destined for the maintenance of the state, have some advantages, which may serve in some measure to balance their inconveniency. When destined for the maintenance of the church, they are attended with nothing but inconveniency.
p62.zh: 在亚洲,这种土地税据说对主权者来说是有兴趣改善和耕种土地的。 因此,据说,中国的君主,即孟加拉人在马荷曼戈文特统治时期的君主,以及古埃及的君主,都极为关注建造和维护良好的道路和通航运河,以便尽可能增加土地每一部分产品的数量和价值,向每一部分购买他们自己的领地所能负担的最广泛的市场。教堂的基座被划分为如此小的部分,以至于其所有者中没有人能有任何这种利益. 一个教区的教长永远找不到他的账户,在修筑一条道路或运河到一个遥远的地方,以便扩大他自己特定教区的农产品市场。 这种税收,当注定要维持国家时,具有一些好处,在某种程度上可能有利于平衡它们的不方便. 当注定要维持教堂时,他们只受到不便的照料。

p63.original: Taxes upon the produce of land may be levied, either in kind, or, according to a certain valuation in money.
p63.zh: 对土地的产值征税,可以实物征收,也可以按照一定的货币价值征收.

p64.original: The parson of a parish, or a gentleman of small fortune who lives upon his estate, may sometimes, perhaps find some advantage in receiving, the one his tythe, and the other his rent, in kind. The quantity to be collected, and the district within which it is to be collected, are so small, that they both can oversee, with their own eyes, the collection and disposal of every part of what is due to them. A gentleman of great fortune, who lived in the capital, would be in danger of suffering much by the neglect, and more by the fraud, of his factors and agents, if the rents of an estate in a distant province were to be paid to him in this manner. The loss of the sovereign, from the abuse and depredation of his tax-gatherers, would necessarily be much greater. The servants of the most careless private person are, perhaps, more under the eye of their master than those of the most careful prince; and a public revenue, which was paid in kind, would suffer so much from the mismanagement of the collectors, that a very small part of what was levied upon the people would ever arrive at the treasury of the prince. Some part of the public revenue of China, however, is said to be paid in this manner. The mandarins and other tax-gatherers will, no doubt, find their advantage in continuing the practice of a payment, which is so much more liable to abuse than any payment in money.
p64.zh: 教区牧师,或住在他庄园里的小财官,有时,也许在接受他的财产和房租方面有一定优势。所要收集的数量,以及所要收集的地区,都太小了,他们两个都能够用自己的眼光监督,来收集和处置每一部分应得的东西.君子大富贵,居京城,若以此法付远省庄园之租,则其因人及代理人之疏忽,更以欺诈为甚,必有受苦之虞.主权者因滥用和掠夺其税收者而丧失的必然要大得多。 最粗心的私人的仆人,也许比最谨慎的王子的仆人更在主人的眼皮底下;而以实物支付的公共收入,会因收藏家的管理不善而大受损失,以至于征收给人民的钱的极小部分会到达王子的国库. 然而,据说中国的部分公共收入是以这种方式支付的。 毫无疑问,普通话和其他税收征收者会发现他们继续支付的做法的好处,这种做法比任何金钱支付都容易被滥用。

p65.original: A tax upon the produce of land, which is levied in money, may be levied, either according to a valuation, which varies with all the variations of the market price; or according to a fixed valuation, a bushel of wheat, for example, being always valued at one and the same money price, whatever may be the state of the market. The produce of a tax levied in the former way will vary only according to the variations in the real produce of the land, according to the improvement or neglect of cultivation. The produce of a tax levied in the latter way will vary, not only according to the variations in the produce of the land, but according both to those in the value of the precious metals, and those in the quantity of those metals which is at different times contained in coin of the same denomination. The produce of the former will always bear the same proportion to the value of the real produce of the land. The produce of the latter may, at different times, bear very different proportions to that value.
p65.zh: 对土地生产征收的税,可以按照市场价格的各种变化,根据估价征收;或者根据固定估价,例如,一毛小麦总按同一货币价格估价,无论市场状况如何。以前一种方式征收的税的产物,只因土地实际产物的变异,因种植的改良或忽视而异.以后一种方式征收的税款的产值将有所不同,不仅取决于土地产值的变化,而且取决于贵金属价值的价值,也取决于不同时期同一面额硬币所含的金属数量。前者的产物将永远承担着与该土地实际产物价值相同的比例.后者的产物在不同的时间可能与这种价值有非常不同的比例。

p66.original: When, instead either of a certain portion of the produce of land, or of the price of a certain portion, a certain sum of money is to be paid in full compensation for all tax or tythe; the tax becomes, in this case, exactly of the same nature with the land tax of England. It neither rises nor falls with the rent of the land. It neither encourages nor discourages improvement. The tythe in the greater part of those parishes which pay what is called a modus, in lieu of all other tythe is a tax of this kind. During the Mahometan government of Bengal, instead of the payment in kind of the fifth part of the produce, a modus, and, it is said, a very moderate one, was established in the greater part of the districts or zemindaries of the country. Some of the servants of the East India company, under pretence of restoring the public revenue to its proper value, have, in some provinces, exchanged this modus for a payment in kind. Under their management, this change is likely both to discourage cultivation, and to give new opportunities for abuse in the collection of the public revenue, which has fallen very much below what it was said to have been when it first fell under the management of the company. The servants of the company may, perhaps, have profited by the change, but at the expense, it is probable, both of their masters and of the country.
p66.zh: 当不是某部分土地的产物,就是某部分土地的价格时,一定数额的钱要全额补偿所有税费或tythe;在此情况下,该税与英格兰的土地税性质完全相同.既不与地租俱升降. 它既不鼓励也不阻碍改进。大部分教区支付所谓的临时款 代替其他所有款的款是这种税 在孟加拉马荷马丹政府执政期间,除了以实物支付第五部分的农产品外,还在该国大部分地区或政府建立了一种临时办法,而且据说是一种非常温和的办法。东印度公司的一些雇员以恢复公共收入的适当价值为借口,在一些省份将这种临时付款换成实物。在其管理下,这一变化可能既会阻止种植,又会给在征收公共收入方面造成新的滥用机会,而公共收入远远低于最初由公司管理时所说的水平。公司的仆人也许已经从变化中获利,但以代价为代价,无论主人还是国家都有可能.

p67.original: Taxes upon the Rent of Houses.

p68.original: The rent of a house may be distinguished into two parts, of which the one may very properly be called the building-rent; the other is commonly called the ground-rent.
p68.zh: 房屋的租金可以分为两部分,其中一部分可能非常恰当地称为建筑租金;另一部分通常称为地租.

p69.original: The building-rent is the interest or profit of the capital expended in building the house. In order to put the trade of a builder upon a level with other trades, it is necessary that this rent should be sufficient, first, to pay him the same interest which he would have got for his capital, if he had lent it upon good security; and, secondly, to keep the house in constant repair, or, what comes to the same thing, to replace, within a certain term of years, the capital which had been employed in building it. The building-rent, or the ordinary profit of building, is, therefore, everywhere regulated by the ordinary interest of money. Where the market rate of interest is four per cent. the rent of a house, which, over and above paying the ground-rent, affords six or six and a-half per cent. upon the whole expense of building, may, perhaps, afford a sufficient profit to the builder. Where the market rate of interest is five per cent. it may perhaps require seven or seven and a half per cent. If, in proportion to the interest of money, the trade of the builders affords at any time much greater profit than this, it will soon draw so much capital from other trades as will reduce the profit to its proper level. If it affords at any time much less than this, other trades will soon draw so much capital from it as will again raise that profit.
p69.zh: 房屋租金是房屋建造所花费的资本的利息或利润。 为了使建筑商的贸易与其他行业达到一定水平,这种租金必须足够,首先,支付他本来会为他资本得到的同样利息,如果他在良好的安全条件下出借的话;其次,使房子不断修理,或者说,同样的事情,在一定的年限内,取代曾经受雇于建造它的资本. 因此,建筑租金,或建筑的普通利润,在任何地方都受到金钱的普通利益管制。 在市场利率为4%的地方,房屋租金,除支付地租外,还支付六或六半的租金,从整个建筑费用来看,也许可以给建筑商带来足够的利润。 如果市场利率为5%,则可能需要7%或7%半的利率。 如果按货币利益的比例计算,建造者的贸易在任何时候都能提供比这大得多的利润,那么它很快将从其他贸易中提取这么多资本,从而将利润降低到适当的水平. 如果它随时能提供比这少得多的资金,其他行业很快会从中提取如此之多的资金,从而再次增加利润。

p70.original: Whatever part of the whole rent of a house is over and above what is sufficient for affording this reasonable profit, naturally goes to the ground-rent; and, where the owner of the ground and the owner of the building are two different persons, is, in most cases, completely paid to the former. This surplus rent is the price which the inhabitant of the house pays for some real or supposed advantage of the situation. In country houses, at a distance from any great town, where there is plenty of ground to chuse upon, the ground-rent is scarce anything, or no more than what the ground which the house stands upon would pay, if employed in agriculture. In country villas, in the neighbourhood of some great town, it is sometimes a good deal higher; and the peculiar conveniency or beauty of situation is there frequently very well paid for. Ground-rents are generally highest in the capital, and in those particular parts of it where there happens to be the greatest demand for houses, whatever be the reason of that demand, whether for trade and business, for pleasure and society, or for mere vanity and fashion.
p70.zh: 房屋租金的无论部分是否超过足以支付合理利润的部分,自然都属于地租;如果地主和建筑主是两个不同的人,则在大多数情况下完全付给前者。 这种剩余租金是住房居民为某种实际或假定的有利条件付出的代价。 在乡间房屋中,在远离任何大城市的地方,如果有充足的土地可以使用,地租就少不了任何东西,或者说,如果受雇于农业,房屋的地价不会超过房子的地价。 在乡村别墅,在一些大城镇的街区,有时会高得多;而且情况的特殊性或优美性往往报酬很高。地租一般在首都最高,在那些对房屋的需求最强的特定地区,无论这种需求的原因是什么,无论是对贸易和商业的需求,还是对享乐和社会的需求,还是对纯粹的虚荣和时尚的需求。

p71.original: A tax upon house-rent, payable by the tenant, and proportioned to the whole rent of each house, could not, for any considerable time at least, affect the building-rent. If the builder did not get his reasonable profit, he would be obliged to quit the trade; which, by raising the demand for building, would, in a short time, bring back his profit to its proper level with that of other trades. Neither would such a tax fall altogether upon the ground-rent; but it would divide itself in such a manner, as to fall partly upon the inhabitant of the house, and partly upon the owner of the ground.
p71.zh: 对房屋租金的征税,由租户支付,并按每所房屋的全部租金按比例计算,至少任何相当长的时间内都不影响房屋租金。 如果建设者没有获得合理利润,他就必须退出贸易;通过提高建设需求,短期内将他的利润与其他行业的利润重新回到适当的水平. 这种税也不可能完全由地租负担;但它会以这样的方式划分自己,一部分落在房屋的居民身上,一部分落在地主身上。

p72.original: Let us suppose, for example, that a particular person judges that he can afford for house-rent all expense of sixty pounds a-year; and let us suppose, too, that a tax of four shillings in the pound, or of one-fifth, payable by the inhabitant, is laid upon house-rent. A house of sixty pounds rent will, in that case, cost him seventy-two pounds a-year, which is twelve pounds more than he thinks he can afford.
