The final payment of this rise of wages, therefore, would, in this case, fall upon the landlord, together with the additional profit of the farmer who had advanced it. In all cases, a direct tax upon the wages of labour must, in the long-run, occasion both a greater reduction in the rent of land, and a greater rise in the price of manufactured goods than would have followed from the proper assessment of a sum equal to the produce of the tax, partly upon the rent of land, and partly upon consumable commodities.
p135.zh: 因此,对劳工工资直接征税,虽然劳工可能从他手中支付,但不能恰当地说,他甚至可以提前征税;至少如果对劳工的需求和规定的平均价格在征税之后保持不变的话。 在所有这些情况下,不仅税收,而且比税收还多的税收,实际上将由立即雇用他的人来推进。在不同情况下,最后付款由不同的人支付。 这种税收在制造业工人工资中可能带来的上涨将由主制造商提出,主制造商既有权也有义务按其商品的价格收取利润。 因此,工资增长的最终支付以及主制造商的额外利润将落在消费者身上。农民可以提高国家劳动工资的这一税收水平,为了维持与以前相同的劳动力数量,农民必须雇用更多的资本。 为了收回这笔更大的资本,加上股票的普通利润,他必须保留更大的部分,或者说,同样的事情,更大的部分的价格,土地的产物,因此,他应该向地主支付更少的租金. 因此,在这种情况下,工资增加的最后支付将落在地主身上,加上提高工资的农民的额外利润。在任何情况下,从长远来看,对劳动工资直接征税必须同时减少土地租金,使制成品价格上涨,比适当评估相当于税款的金额,部分是土地租金,部分是消耗性商品。

p136.original: If direct taxes upon the wages of labour have not always occasioned a proportionable rise in those wages, it is because they have generally occasioned a considerable fall in the demand of labour. The declension of industry, the decrease of employment for the poor, the diminution of the annual produce of the land and labour of the country, have generally been the effects of such taxes. In consequence of them, however, the price of labour must always be higher than it otherwise would have been in the actual state of the demand; and this enhancement of price, together with the profit of those who advance it, must always be finally paid by the landlords and consumers.
p136.zh: 如果说对劳工工资的直接征税并不总是导致这些工资有一定比例的增长,那是因为这些税通常导致劳工需求大幅下降。工业的衰退、穷人就业的减少、国家土地和劳动力的年产量的减少,一般都是这种税收的影响。 然而,由于这些原因,劳动力价格必须总是高于本来会处于实际需求状态的劳动力价格;这种物价的提高,加上推进者利润的提高,必须始终最终由地主和消费者支付。

p137.original: A tax upon the wages of country labour does not raise the price of the rude produce of land in proportion to the tax; for the same reason that a tax upon the farmer's profit does not raise that price in that proportion.
p137.zh: 国家劳动工资税不按税额比例提高粗劣土地产地价格;同样原因,农民利润税不按该比例提高该价格.

p138.original: Absurd and destructive as such taxes are, however, they take place in many countries. In France, that part of the taille which is charged upon the industry of workmen and day-labourers in country villages, is properly a tax of this kind. Their wages are computed according to the common rate of the district in which they reside; and, that they may be as little liable as possible to any overcharge, their yearly gains are estimated at no more than two hundred working days in the year. {Memoires concernant les Droits, etc. tom. ii. p. 108.} The tax of each individual is varied from year to year, according to different circumstances, of which the collector or the commissary, whom intendant appoints to assist him, are the judges. In Bohemia, in consequence of the alteration in the system of finances which was begun in 1748, a very heavy tax is imposed upon the industry of artificers. They are divided into four classes. The highest class pay a hundred florins a year, which, at two-and-twenty pence half penny a-florin, amounts to £9:7:6. The second class are taxed at seventy; the third at fifty; and the fourth, comprehending artificers in villages, and the lowest class of those in towns, at twenty-five florins. {Memoires concemant les Droits, etc. tom. iii. p. 87.}
p138.zh: 然而,在许多国家,这种税收是异常和破坏性的。 在法国,向乡村工人和日工行业收取的部分尾矿是适当的这种税。 他们的工资是根据他们所居住地区的共同费率计算的;而且,他们可能尽可能不承担任何超额收费的责任,估计他们每年的收益每年不超过200个工作日。108. 每个人的税收每年根据不同情况不同而不同,其中法官是收藏家或小卖部,他们打算协助他。 在波希米亚,由于1748年开始的金融系统改变,对艺术家行业征收了非常沉重的税。分为四类.最高班级每年支付100弗罗林,在每弗罗林的两便士和20便士时,相当于9:7:6英镑. 二等税为:七十;三等税为:五十;四等税为:村中通晓文艺者,镇中最低等税为二十五弗罗林. {Memorics concemant les Droits等.iii.p.87] (中文(简体) ).

p139.original: The recompence of ingenious artists, and of men of liberal professions, I have endeavoured to show in the first book, necessarily keeps a certain proportion to the emoluments of inferior trades. A tax upon this recompence, therefore, could have no other effect than to raise it somewhat higher than in proportion to the tax. If it did not rise in this manner, the ingenious arts and the liberal professions, being; no longer upon a level with other trades, would be so much deserted, that they would soon return to that level.
p139.zh: 我努力在第一本书中展现出天才艺术家和自由职业男子的复习精神, 一定保持一定比例的低级行业薪酬。 因此,对这种补偿的征税除了提高该税额比该税额的一定比例之外,没有其他效果。 如果它不以这种方式兴起,那么天才的艺术和自由职业,即现在;不再与其他行业处于一个水平,就会变得如此荒废,以至于很快会恢复到这个水平.

p140.original: The emoluments of offices are not, like those of trades and professions, regulated by the free competition of the market, and do not, therefore, always bear a just proportion to what the nature of the employment requires. They are, perhaps, in most countries, higher than it requires; the persons who have the administration of government being generally disposed to regard both themselves and their immediate dependents, rather more than enough. The emoluments of offices, therefore, can, in most cases, very well bear to be taxed. The persons, besides, who enjoy public offices, especially the more lucrative, are, in all countries, the objects of general envy; and a tax upon their emoluments, even though it should be somewhat higher than upon any other sort of revenue, is always a very popular tax. In England, for example, when, by the land-tax, every other sort of revenue was supposed to be assessed at four shillings in the pound, it was very popular to lay a real tax of five shillings and sixpence in the pound upon the salaries of offices which exceeded a hundred pounds a-year; the pensions of the younger branches of the royal family, the pay of the officers of the army and navy, and a few others less obnoxious to envy, excepted. There are in England no other direct taxes upon the wages of labour.
p140.zh: 办公室的薪酬与行业和专业的薪酬不同,不受市场自由竞争的制约,因此,并不总是与就业性质要求的比例相称。 在大多数国家,他们也许比需要的要高;政府行政部门一般都关心自己及其直系亲属,但还不够。 因此,在大多数情况下,办公室的薪酬非常值得征税。 此外,在所有国家中,担任公职、特别是更有利可图的人都是普遍羡慕的对象;对他们的薪酬征税,尽管应比任何其他种类的收入高一些,但总是非常受欢迎的税。 例如在英国,根据土地税,其他各种收入应该以英镑的4先令来分摊,因此非常流行的是,在每年超过100磅的办公室工资上下5先令和6便士的实际税额;王室较年轻的分支的养老金,陆军和海军军官的薪水,以及少数其他不那么讨厌嫉妒的人,除了.英格兰对劳动工资没有其他的直接税.

p141.original: ARTICLE IV.--Taxes which it is intended should fall indifferently upon every different Species of Revenue.
p141.zh: 第4条 -- -- 其意图的税种应不加区别地落在每一种不同的收入物种身上。

p142.original: The taxes which it is intended should fall indifferently upon every different species of revenue, are capitation taxes, and taxes upon consumable commodities. Those must be paid indifferently, from whatever revenue the contributors may possess; from the rent of their land, from the profits of their stock, or from the wages of their labour.
p142.zh: 其意图的税收应无差别地落在每一种类的收入上,即人均税和消费商品税。 这些工资必须无差别地从缴款者可能拥有的任何收入、土地的租金、库存利润或劳动力的工资中支付。

p144.original: Capitation taxes, if it is attempted to proportion them to the fortune or revenue of each contributor, become altogether arbitrary. The state of a man's fortune varies from day to day; and, without an inquisition, more intolerable than any tax, and renewed at least once every year, can only be guessed at. His assessment, therefore, must, in most cases, depend upon the good or bad humour of his assessors, and must, therefore, be altogether arbitrary and uncertain.
p144.zh: 如果企图将其与每个缴款者的财产或收入相提并论,没收税就完全武断。人财之境,日日各有不同;而无问讯,比任何税,更不能容忍,每年至少续办一次,只能猜到. 因此,在大多数情况下,他的评估必须取决于其陪审员的好坏幽默,因此,评估必须完全武断和不确定。

p145.original: Capitation taxes, if they are proportioned, not to the supposed fortune, but to the rank of each contributor, become altogether unequal; the degrees of fortune being frequently unequal in the same degree of rank.
p145.zh: 赋税如果按比例计算,则不是按假定的财富,而是按每个贡献者的级别计算,就变得完全不平等;在同等级别上,财富的程度常常是不平等的。

p146.original: Such taxes, therefore, if it is attempted to render them equal, become altogether arbitrary and uncertain; and if it is attempted to render them certain and not arbitrary, become altogether unequal. Let the tax be light or heavy, uncertainty is always a great grievance. In a light tax, a considerable degree of inequality may be supported; in a heavy one, it is altogether intolerable.
p146.zh: 因此,如果试图使这些税制平等,就变得完全武断和不确定;如果试图使这些税制具有确定性而不是任意性,就变得完全不平等。 让税收变得轻或重,不确定性总是一个巨大的冤情. 在轻税中,可以支持相当程度的不平等;在重税中,这种不平等是完全不能容忍的。

p147.original: In the different poll-taxes which took place in England during the reign of William III. the contributors were, the greater part of them, assessed according to the degree of their rank; as dukes, marquises, earls, viscounts, barons, esquires, gentlemen, the eldest and youngest sons of peers, etc. All shop-keepers and tradesmen worth more than three hundred pounds, that is, the better sort of them, were subject to the same assessment, how great soever might be the difference in their fortunes. Their rank was more considered than their fortune. Several of those who, in the first poll-tax, were rated according to their supposed fortune were afterwards rated according to their rank. Serjeants, attorneys, and proctors at law, who, in the first poll-tax, were assessed at three shillings in the pound of their supposed income, were afterwards assessed as gentlemen. In the assessment of a tax which was not very heavy, a considerable degree of inequality had been found less insupportable than any degree of uncertainty.
p147.zh: 在威廉三世统治时期发生在英国的不同民意调查税中,贡献者多半是根据其等级等级评定的;作为公爵,侯爵,耳 ⁇ ,子爵,男爵,侍从,绅士,同辈的长子和幼子等. 所有店员和商人 价值超过三百磅, 也就是他们中最好的一种, 都受到同样的评估, 不论谁 都可能是他们财富的差别。 他们的军衔比他们的财富更受考虑. 在第一个民意调查税中,根据自己推测的财富评级的几个人随后根据自己的级别评级.公务员、律师和律师,在第一次投票税中,他们被评估为3先令,相当于他们预期收入的英镑,后来被评为绅士。 在评估不是非常沉重的税额时,发现相当程度的不平等不如任何程度的不确定性所支持。

p148.original: In the capitation which has been levied in France, without-any interruption, since the beginning of the present century, the highest orders of people are rated according to their rank, by an invariable tariff; the lower orders of people, according to what is supposed to be their fortune, by an assessment which varies from year to year. The officers of the king's court, the judges, and other officers in the superior courts of justice, the officers of the troops, etc are assessed in the first manner. The inferior ranks of people in the provinces are assessed in the second. In France, the great easily submit to a considerable degree of inequality in a tax which, so far as it affects them, is not a very heavy one; but could not brook the arbitrary assessment of an intendant.
p148.zh: 在自本世纪初以来,在法国征收的人均税额中,人们的最高等级按其等级、不可改变的关税加以评定;人们的较低等级按其应得财富加以评定,其等级每年有所不同。御史中丞的官吏,判官,高等司法院的其他官吏,部队的官吏等,均以第一方式评定.各省的低级人口等级在第二批中评定. 在法国,极容易在税收方面面临相当程度的不平等,而这种不平等对他们的影响并不很大;但是不能消除对意图者的任意评估。

p149.original: The inferior ranks of people must, in that country, suffer patiently the usage which their superiors think proper to give them.
p149.zh: 在该国,低等阶层的人必须耐心地承受其上级认为应该给予他们的习惯。

p150.original: In England, the different poll-taxes never produced the sum which had been expected from them, or which it was supposed they might have produced, had they been exactly levied. In France, the capitation always produces the sum expected from it. The mild government of England, when it assessed the different ranks of people to the poll-tax, contented itself with what that assessment happened to produce, and required no compensation for the loss which the state might sustain, either by those who could not pay, or by those who would not pay (for there were many such), and who, by the indulgent execution of the law, were not forced to pay. The more severe government of France assesses upon each generality a certain sum, which the intendant must find as he can. If any province complains of being assessed too high, it may, in the assessment of next year, obtain an abatement proportioned to the overcharge of the year before; but it must pay in the mean time. The intendant, in order to be sure of finding the sum assessed upon his generality, was empowered to assess it in a larger sum, that the failure or inability of some of the contributors might be compensated by the overcharge of the rest; and till 1765, the fixation of this surplus assessment was left altogether to his discretion. In that year, indeed, the council assumed this power to itself. In the capitation of the provinces, it is observed by the perfectly well informed author of the Memoirs upon the Impositions in France, the proportion which falls upon the nobility, and upon those whose privileges exempt them from the taille, is the least considerable. The largest falls upon those subject to the taille, who are assessed to the capitation at so much a-pound of what they pay to that other tax. Capitation taxes, so far as they are levied upon the lower ranks of people, are direct taxes upon the wages of labour, and are attended with all the inconveniencies of such taxes.
p150.zh: 在英国,不同的民意调查税从未产生过他们预期得到的金额,或者它们可能已经产生的数量,如果它们被完全征收的话。 在法国,人均总能产生预期的金额。温和的英国政府在对不同阶层的人进行投票税评估时,满足于评估所产生的结果,不需要对国家可能承受的损失作出赔偿,无论是那些无力支付的人,还是那些不愿支付的人(因为有许多这样的人),而且由于法律的放纵执行,他们没有被迫支付。更严厉的法国政府会评估每一普遍情况,计划者必须尽可能找到一笔款项。 如果任何省份抱怨评估过高,在下一年度的评估中,它可以获得与上一年多收费用成比例的减额;但必须在平均时间内支付。 为了确定根据他的一般情况确定所分摊的数额,打算者有权评估数额较大的数额,即某些缴款国的失败或无力可能由其他缴款者多收的费用来补偿;直到1765年,这笔盈余摊款完全由他自行决定。 当年,实际上,议会掌握了这一权力。 在各省的人均数字中,法国印地安人备忘录的完全知情作者观察到,贵族和特权豁免他们尾巴的人的比例最低。最大的是受尾矿管制的人,他们按他们付给其他税的一磅的人均计算。 对下层人民征收的赋能税是对劳动工资直接征税,并伴随着这种税的各种不便。

p151.original: Capitation taxes are levied at little expense; and, where they are rigorously exacted, afford a very sure revenue to the state. It is upon this account that, in countries where the case, comfort, and security of the inferior ranks of people are little attended to, capitation taxes are very common. It is in general, however, but a small part of the public revenue, which, in a great empire, has ever been drawn from such taxes; and the greatest sum which they have ever afforded, might always have been found in some other way much more convenient to the people.
p151.zh: 征收赋能税的费用很少;在严格征收赋能税的情况下,国家可以提供非常可靠的收入。 正是基于这一理由,在低等人群的舒适和安全得不到重视的国家,人均税非常普遍。 然而,总的来说,它只是公共收入的一小部分,在一个大帝国中,这种收入曾经从这种税收中抽出;而且,它们提供的最大数额,可能总是以某种其他方式对人民更加方便。

p153.original: The impossibility of taxing the people, in proportion to their revenue, by any capitation, seems to have given occasion to the invention of taxes upon consumable commodities. The state not knowing how to tax, directly and proportionably, the revenue of its subjects, endeavours to tax it indirectly by taxing their expense, which, it is supposed, will, in most cases, be nearly in proportion to their revenue. Their expense is taxed, by taxing the consumable commodities upon which it is laid out.
p153.zh: 无法按收入比例对人民征税,这似乎为发明消费商品征税提供了机会。国家不知道如何直接和按比例地对国民的收入征税,因此试图通过对国民开支征税间接征税,据推测,在大多数情况下,这种征税将接近于国民收入的比例。其费用通过对它所依据的消耗性商品征税来征税。

p154.original: Consumable commodities are either necessaries or luxuries.
p154.zh: 消费商品要么是必需品,要么是奢侈品。

p155.original: By necessaries I understand, not only the commodities which are indispensibly necessary for the support of life, but whatever the custom of the country renders it indecent for creditable people, even of the lowest order, to be without. A linen shirt, for example, is, strictly speaking, not a necessary of life. The Greeks and Romans lived, I suppose, very comfortably, though they had no linen. But in the present times, through the greater part of Europe, a creditable day-labourer would be ashamed to appear in public without a linen shirt, the want of which would be supposed to denote that disgraceful degree of poverty, which, it is presumed, nobody can well fall into without extreme bad conduct. Custom, in the same manner, has rendered leather shoes a necessary of life in England. The poorest creditable person, of either sex, would be ashamed to appear in public without them. In Scotland, custom has rendered them a necessary of life to the lowest order of men; but not to the same order of women, who may, without any discredit, walk about barefooted. In France, they are necessaries neither to men nor to women; the lowest rank of both sexes appearing there publicly, without any discredit, sometimes in wooden shoes, and sometimes barefooted. Under necessaries, therefore, I comprehend, not only those things which nature, but those things which the established rules of decency have rendered necessary to the lowest rank of people. All other things I call luxuries, without meaning, by this appellation, to throw the smallest degree of reproach upon the temperate use of them. Beer and ale, for example, in Great Britain, and wine, even in the wine countries, I call luxuries. A man of any rank may, without any reproach, abstain totally from tasting such liquors. Nature does not render them necessary for the support of life; and custom nowhere renders it indecent to live without them.
p155.zh: 我理解,不仅为了维持生活所必不可少的商品,而且无论国家习俗如何,让那些值得信赖的人,即使是最底层的人,都不能享受到这些商品。 例如亚麻衬衫严格来说,并不是生活的必要. 希腊人和罗马人 生活得很舒适 虽然他们没有亚麻布 但是在当今的时代,通过欧洲大部分地区,一个值得称道的日工会感到羞耻,没有亚麻衬衫就出现在公众面前,而亚麻衬衫的渴望应该意味着这种可耻的贫困程度,而据推测,如果没有极端的恶劣行为,任何人都不可能陷入这种贫困。风俗习惯同样使皮鞋在英国成为生活必需.不论男女,最贫穷的可资信赖的人,如果没有他们,都会羞愧地出现在公众面前。 在苏格兰,习俗使他们成为最低的男性秩序所必须的生活;但是,与妇女秩序不同,她们可以赤脚走动,而没有任何名誉。 在法国,她们既不是男人也不是女人所必须的;在法国,她们是公开露面的男女中地位最低的,没有任何信誉,有时穿木鞋,有时赤脚。 因此,我理解的不仅是那些自然的东西,还有那些既定的体面规则为最低层人民所必需的东西。 我称之为奢侈品的所有其他东西,没有意义,通过这个称呼,来给它们温和的使用以最小程度的责难.啤酒和啤酒,例如在大不列颠,还有葡萄酒,甚至在葡萄酒国,我称之为奢侈酒.任何级别的人可以毫无指责地 完全不喝这种酒自然不能使他们成为维持生命的必要条件;没有他们的习惯,没有他们的习惯,生活就变得不体面。

p156.original: As the wages of labour are everywhere regulated, partly by the demand for it, and partly by the average price of the necessary articles of subsistence; whatever raises this average price must necessarily raise those wages; so that the labourer may still be able to purchase that quantity of those necessary articles which the state of the demand for labour, whether increasing, stationary, or declining, requires that he should have. {See book i.chap. 8} A tax upon those articles necessarily raises their price somewhat higher than the amount of the tax, because the dealer, who advances the tax, must generally get it back, with a profit. Such a tax must, therefore, occasion a rise in the wages of labour, proportionable to this rise of price.
p156.zh: 由于各地都对劳工工资实行管制,部分受对工资的需求,部分受生活必需品平均价格的管制;无论提高这种平均价格,都必须提高这些工资;这样,劳工仍然可能能够购买那些劳动力需求状况要求他必须购买的必要物品的数量,无论是增加、固定还是下降。8) 对这些物品的征税必然会使其价格比征税额高一些,因为提税的经销商一般必须收回,并有利润。 因此,这种税收必须导致与这种价格上涨相称的劳动工资上升。

p157.original: It is thus that a tax upon the necessaries of life operates exactly in the same manner as a direct tax upon the wages of labour. The labourer, though he may pay it out of his hand, cannot, for any considerable time at least, be properly said even to advance it. It must always, in the long-run, be advanced to him by his immediate employer, in the advanced state of wages. His employer, if he is a manufacturer, will charge upon the price of his goods the rise of wages, together with a profit, so that the final payment of the tax, together with this overcharge, will fall upon the consumer. If his employer is a farmer, the final payment, together with a like overcharge, will fall upon the rent of the landlord.
p157.zh: 因此,对生活必需品的征税与对劳工工资的直接征税完全相同。工人虽然可以自掏腰包,但至少在任何相当长的时间内,都不能说是适当的,甚至不能说是为了推进这项工作。 从长远来看,必须始终由他的直属雇主,在工资的先进状态下,向他推进. 他的雇主,如果他是制造商,将向其商品的价格收取工资上涨和利润,这样,最后的税款支付,加上这种超额收费,将落在消费者身上。 如果他的雇主是农民,最后的付款以及类似的多收费用将落在房东的租金上。

p158.original: It is otherwise with taxes upon what I call luxuries, even upon those of the poor. The rise in the price of the taxed commodities, will not necessarily occasion any rise in the wages of labour. A tax upon tobacco, for example, though a luxury of the poor, as well as of the rich, will not raise wages. Though it is taxed in England at three times, and in France at fifteen times its original price, those high duties seem to have no effect upon the wages of labour. The same thing maybe said of the taxes upon tea and sugar, which, in England and Holland, have become luxuries of the lowest ranks of people; and of those upon chocolate, which, in Spain, is said to have become so.
p158.zh: 否则,我所说的奢侈品,即使是穷人的奢侈品,都要征税。所税商品价格上涨不一定会引起劳动工资的任何上涨。 例如,对烟草征税,虽然对穷人和富人来说是奢侈品,但不会提高工资。 虽然在英国征税三次,在法国征税十五次,但这些高额关税似乎对劳动工资没有影响。茶和糖的税也许也一样,在英国和荷兰,茶和糖已经成为最低层人群的奢侈品;在巧克力的税中,据说在西班牙,这种税也变成了奢侈品。

p159.original: The different taxes which, in Great Britain, have, in the course of the present century, been imposed upon spiritous liquors, are not supposed to have had any effect upon the wages of labour. The rise in the price of porter, occasioned by an additional tax of three shillings upon the barrel of strong beer, has not raised the wages of common labour in London. These were about eighteen pence or twenty pence a-day before the tax, and they are not more now.
p159.zh: 在大不列颠,在本世纪期间,对烈酒征收的不同税种不应对劳动工资产生任何影响。搬运工的价格上涨,加上对强力啤酒桶额外征收三先令的税,并没有提高伦敦普通劳工的工资. 这些是在征税前一天18便士或20便士,现在不是了。

p160.original: The high price of such commodities does not necessarily diminish the ability of the inferior ranks of people to bring up families. Upon the sober and industrious poor, taxes upon such commodities act as sumptuary laws, and dispose them either to moderate, or to refrain altogether from the use of superfluities which they can no longer easily afford. Their ability to bring up families, in consequence of this forced frugality, instead of being diminished, is frequently, perhaps, increased by the tax. It is the sober and industrious poor who generally bring up the most numerous families, and who principally supply the demand for useful labour. All the poor, indeed, are not sober and industrious; and the dissolute and disorderly might continue to indulge themselves in the use of such commodities, after this rise of price, in the same manner as before, without regarding the distress which this indulgence might bring upon their families. Such disorderly persons, however, seldom rear up numerous families, their children generally perishing from neglect, mismanagement, and the scantiness or unwholesomeness of their food. If by the strength of their constitution, they survive the hardships to which the bad conduct of their parents exposes them, yet the example of that bad conduct commonly corrupts their morals; so that, instead of being useful to society by their industry, they become public nuisances by their vices and disorders. Through the advanced price of the luxuries of the poor, therefore, might increase somewhat the distress of such disorderly families, and thereby diminish somewhat their ability to bring up children, it would not probably diminish much the useful population of the country.
p160.zh: 此类商品的高价格并不一定会削弱低层阶层的人抚养家庭的能力。 在清醒和勤奋的穷人身上,对这些商品的征税成为了自以为是的法律,要么予以缓和,要么完全避免使用他们不再容易承受的超级流利。 由于这种强制节俭,她们养育家庭的能力不是被削弱,而是经常因税收而增加。 一般是清醒和勤奋的穷人抚养着数量最多的家庭,他们主要提供对有用劳动力的需求。 实际上,所有穷人都不是清醒和勤奋的;在价格上涨之后,这种无节制和无序的状态可能象以前一样,继续放任使用这种商品,而不考虑这种放任可能给其家人带来的痛苦。 然而,这种无序的人很少养活许多家庭,他们的孩子一般都死于忽视、管理不善、食物少或不卫生。 如果凭借其宪法的力量,他们能够忍受父母的不良行为暴露给他们带来的困难,然而,这种不良行为的例子通常会损害他们的道德;这样,他们就不是因为自己的行业对社会有用,而是因为自己的恶习和失调而成为公众的麻烦。 因此,通过穷人奢侈品的先进价格,可能会增加这些无序家庭的痛苦,从而在一定程度上削弱他们抚养子女的能力,这很可能不会大大削弱该国有用的人口。

p161.original: Any rise in the average price of necessaries, unless it be compensated by a proportionable rise in the wages of labour, must necessarily diminish, more or less, the ability of the poor to bring up numerous families, and, consequently, to supply the demand for useful labour; whatever may be the state of that demand, whether increasing, stationary, or declining; or such as requires an increasing, stationary, or declining population.
p161.zh: 必要人员平均价格的任何上涨,除非以合理的劳动工资上涨来补偿,必然会多少削弱穷人抚养众多家庭的能力,从而满足对有用劳动力的需求;无论这种需求状况如何,无论是增加、固定、还是下降;或者需要增加、固定或减少人口。

p162.original: Taxes upon luxuries have no tendency to raise the price of any other commodities, except that of the commodities taxed. Taxes upon necessaries, by raising the wages of labour, necessarily tend to raise the price of all manufactures, and consequently to diminish the extent of their sale and consumption. Taxes upon luxuries are finally paid by the consumers of the commodities taxed, without any retribution. They fall indifferently upon every species of revenue, the wages of labour, the profits of stock, and the rent of land. Taxes upon necessaries, so far as they affect the labouring poor, are finally paid, partly by landlords, in the diminished rent of their lands, and partly by rich consumers, whether landlords or others, in the advanced price of manufactured goods; and always with a considerable overcharge. The advanced price of such manufactures as are real necessaries of life, and are destined for the consumption of the poor, of coarse woollens, for example, must be compensated to the poor by a farther advancement of their wages. The middling and superior ranks of people, if they understood their own interest, ought always to oppose all taxes upon the necessaries of life, as well as all taxes upon the wages of labour. The final payment of both the one and the other falls altogether upon themselves, and always with a considerable overcharge. They fall heaviest upon the landlords, who always pay in a double capacity; in that of landlords, by the reduction, of their rent; and in that of rich consumers, by the increase of their expense. The observation of Sir Matthew Decker, that certain taxes are, in the price of certain goods, sometimes repeated and accumulated four or five times, is perfectly just with regard to taxes upon the necessaries of life. In the price of leather, for example, you must pay not only for the tax upon the leather of your own shoes, but for a part of that upon those of the shoemaker and the tanner. You must pay, too, for the tax upon the salt, upon the soap, and upon the candles which those workmen consume while employed in your service; and for the tax upon the leather, which the saltmaker, the soap-maker, and the candle-maker consume, while employed in their service.
p162.zh: 对奢侈品的征税除了对所征税的商品外,没有其他商品的价格上涨的趋势。 通过提高劳动工资,对必要产品征税必然会提高所有制成品的价格,从而减少其销售和消费。 对奢侈品的征税最终由所征税项的商品的消费者支付,没有任何报复.收入、工资、股票利润和土地租金无差别地落在每一种类的收入上。 对必要人员征税,只要影响到贫穷劳动者,最终由地主支付,部分由地主支付,部分由土地租金减少,部分由富裕消费者支付,无论是地主还是其他人,其制成品的先进价格;而且总要收取相当高的超额费用。诸如粗羊毛等真正生活必需品和供穷人消费的制成品的先进价格,必须通过进一步提高穷人的工资来补偿穷人。干涉和优越的阶层,如果理解他们自己的利益,就应该永远反对对生活必需品征收的一切税,以及对劳动工资征收的一切税。一方和另一方的最终付款完全由自己支付,而且总是要收取相当高的超额费用。 他们最重的落在地主身上,他们总是以双重能力支付;在地主身上,通过减少租金;在富人身上,通过增加开支。 马修·德克爵士的观察,在某些商品的价格上,某些税有时重复和积累了四五次,这在生活必需品的税收方面是完全公正的. 例如皮革的价格,你不仅必须支付自己鞋子皮革的税费,而且必须支付鞋匠和制革师皮革的部分税费.亦须交纳盐税,肥皂税,工人们在为您服务时所消耗的蜡烛税;及盐匠,肥皂匠,蜡烛匠在为您服务时所消耗的皮革税.

p163.original: In Great Britain, the principal taxes upon the necessaries of life, are those upon the four commodities just now mentioned, salt, leather, soap, and candles.
p163.zh: 在大不列颠,生活必需品的主要税收是刚刚提到的四种商品,即盐、皮革、肥皂和蜡烛。

p164.original: Salt is a very ancient and a very universal subject of taxation. It was taxed among the Romans, and it is so at present in, I believe, every part of Europe. The quantity annually consumed by any individual is so small, and may be purchased so gradually, that nobody, it seems to have been thought, could feel very sensibly even a pretty heavy tax upon it. It is in England taxed at three shillings and fourpence a bushel; about three times the original price of the commodity. In some other countries, the tax is still higher. Leather is a real necessary of life. The use of linen renders soap such. In countries where the winter nights are long, candles are a necessary instrument of trade. Leather and soap are in Great Britain taxed at three halfpence a-pound; candles at a penny; taxes which, upon the original price of leather, may amount to about eight or ten per cent.; upon that of soap, to about twenty or five-and-twenty per cent.; and upon that of candles to about fourteen or fifteen per cent.; taxes which, though lighter than that upon salt, are still very heavy. As all those four commodities are real necessaries of life, such heavy taxes upon them must increase somewhat the expense of the sober and industrious poor, and must consequently raise more or less the wages of their labour.
p164.zh: 盐是一个非常古老和非常普遍的税收主体.罗马人之间曾征税, 我相信,目前在欧洲的每一个地区都是如此。任何个人每年消费的数量如此之少,而且可能如此逐步地购买,似乎没有人会觉得,即使是对它征收相当沉重的税,也非常明智。 在英国,它以3先令和4便士的一匹灌木;大约是该商品的原价的3倍。 在另一些国家,税收仍然较高。皮革是生命中真正的必要内容.使用亚麻使肥皂变得如此. 在冬季夜长的国家,蜡烛是贸易的必要工具. 在英国,皮革和肥皂的税额为每磅三便士;蜡烛的税额为一分钱;根据皮革的原价,其税额可达约8%或10%;在肥皂的税额为约20%或5%或20%;在蜡烛的税额为约14%或15%;虽然比盐的税额要轻,但税额仍然非常沉重。 由于这四种商品都是真正的生活必需品,因此,对他们征收的如此重的税必须在一定程度上增加清醒和勤奋的穷人的开支,因此,必须多多少少地提高他们的劳动工资。

p165.original: In a country where the winters are so cold as in Great Britain, fuel is, during that season, in the strictest sense of the word, a necessary of life, not only for the purpose of dressing victuals, but for the comfortable subsistence of many different sorts of workmen who work within doors; and coals are the cheapest of all fuel. The price of fuel has so important an influence upon that of labour, that all over Great Britain, manufactures have confined themselves principally to the coal counties; other parts of the country, on account of the high price of this necessary article, not being able to work so cheap. In some manufactures, besides, coal is a necessary instrument of trade; as in those of glass, iron, and all other metals. If a bounty could in any case be reasonable, it might perhaps be so upon the transportation of coals from those parts of the country in which they abound, to those in which they are wanted. But the legislature, instead of a bounty, has imposed a tax of three shillings and threepence a-ton upon coals carried coastways; which, upon most sorts of coal, is more than sixty per cent. of the original price at the coal pit. Coals carried, either by land or by inland navigation, pay no duty. Where they are naturally cheap, they are consumed duty free; where they are naturally dear, they are loaded with a heavy duty.
p165.zh: 在一个冬季寒冷如大不列颠的国家,燃料在这个季节里,在最严格意义上来说,是生活的必要条件,不仅是为了穿戴维他命,而且是为了许多不同种类的工人在门内工作的舒适生活;煤是所有燃料中最便宜的.燃料价格对劳动力有如此重要的影响,以至于整个大不列颠的制造业主要局限于煤炭县;由于这一必要物品价格高昂,该国其他地区无法如此廉价地工作。 此外,在一些制成品中,煤炭是贸易的必要工具;在玻璃、铁和所有其他金属中也是如此。 如果一笔赏金在任何情况下都是合理的,那么,从煤炭泛滥的国家那些地区向被通缉者运送煤炭,或许也是如此。 但是,立法机关没有给予任何赏金,而是对运入海岸的煤炭征收3先令和3便士一吨的税;对大多数类型的煤炭来说,这比煤矿原价的60%多。携带的煤炭,无论是陆路还是内河航行,都不缴税. 凡自然便宜者,其消耗免关税;自然珍贵者,其载重税.

p166.original: Such taxes, though they raise the price of subsistence, and consequently the wages of labour, yet they afford a considerable revenue to government, which it might not be easy to find in any other way. There may, therefore, be good reasons for continuing them. The bounty upon the exportation of corn, so far us it tends, in the actual state of tillage, to raise the price of that necessary article, produces all the like bad effects; and instead of affording any revenue, frequently occasions a very great expense to government. The high duties upon the importation of foreign corn, which, in years of moderate plenty, amount to a prohibition; and the absolute prohibition of the importation, either of live cattle, or of salt provisions, which takes place in the ordinary state of the law, and which, on account of the scarcity, is at present suspended for a limited time with regard to Ireland and the British plantations, have all had the bad effects of taxes upon the necessaries of life, and produce no revenue to government. Nothing seems necessary for the repeal of such regulations, but to convince the public of the futility of that system in consequence of which they have been established.
p166.zh: 这种税收虽然提高了维持生计的价格,因而提高了劳动工资,但却为政府提供了相当可观的收入,而以任何其他方式可能都不容易找到。 因此,可能有充分的理由继续这样做。 对出口玉米的赏金,到目前为止,我们往往在耕作的实际状态下,提高这一必要物品的价格,从而产生各种类似坏后果;而且,不但没有提供任何收入,而且经常给政府带来巨大的开支。进口外国玉米的关税很高,在数量中等的年份,相当于禁止进口;绝对禁止进口活牛或食盐,这是在正常的法律状态下进行的,而且由于短缺,目前对爱尔兰和英国种植园暂停了有限的时间,所有这些都对生活必需品产生了税收的不良影响,没有给政府带来收入。似乎没有必要废除这些条例,而只能使公众相信,建立这种制度是徒劳无益的。

p167.original: Taxes upon the necessaries of life are much higher in many other countries than in Great Britain. Duties upon flour and meal when ground at the mill, and upon bread when baked at the oven, take place in many countries. In Holland the money-price of the: bread consumed in towns is supposed to be doubled by means of such taxes. In lieu of a part of them, the people who live in the country, pay every year so much a-head, according to the sort of bread they are supposed to consume. Those who consume wheaten bread pay three guilders fifteen stivers; about six shillings and ninepence halfpenny. Those, and some other taxes of the same kind, by raising the price of labour, are said to have ruined the greater part of the manufactures of Holland {Memoires concernant les Droits, etc. p. 210, 211.}. Similar taxes, though not quite so heavy, take place in the Milanese, in the states of Genoa, in the duchy of Modena, in the duchies of Parma, Placentia, and Guastalla, and the Ecclesiastical state. A French author {Le Reformateur} of some note, has proposed to reform the finances of his country, by substituting in the room of the greater part of other taxes, this most ruinous of all taxes. There is nothing so absurd, says Cicero, which has not sometimes been asserted by some philosophers.
p167.zh: 生活必需品的税收在很多其他国家比在大不列颠高得多。在许多国家,面粉和面粉在磨坊铺设时、面包在烤箱烘烤时都承担义务。 在荷兰,通过征收这种税,城镇消费的面包的价格应该翻一番。住在乡下的人每年要花这么多钱, 而不是用他们应该消费的面包来代替一部分。食用小麦面包的人支付3荷兰盾的15块硬币;大约6先令和9便士半便士。 据说,这些税项和其他一些同类税项通过提高劳动价格,破坏了荷兰的很大一部分制造产品。210, 211.} (中文(简体) ).类似的税收虽然并不那么沉重,但是在米兰,热那亚州,摩德纳州,帕尔马州,普拉森蒂亚州,瓜斯塔拉州,以及教会州的杜奇斯都也有发生. 一位法国作家({Le Reformateur})提议改革国家财政, 西塞罗说,没有什么荒唐的, 某些哲学家有时没有断言这一点。

p168.original: Taxes upon butcher's meat are still more common than those upon bread. It may indeed be doubted, whether butcher's meat is any where a necessary of life. Grain and other vegetables, with the help of milk, cheese, and butter, or oil, where butter is not to be had, it is known from experience, can, without any butcher's meat, afford the most plentiful, the most wholesome, the most nourishing, and the most invigorating diet. Decency nowhere requires that any man should eat butcher's meat, as it in most places requires that he should wear a linen shirt or a pair of leather shoes.
p168.zh: 对屠夫肉类的征税仍然比对面包的征税更为普遍.屠夫的肉是否是生命所必需的,这的确值得怀疑。食粮和其他蔬菜,在牛奶,奶酪,黄油,或油等帮助下,如果黄油不吃,从经验中可以知道,如果没有任何屠夫的肉,可以负担最丰盛,最健康,营养最丰富,最刺激的饮食. 无处可容要求任何人吃屠夫的肉,因为大多数地方都要求他必须穿一件亚麻衬衫或一双皮鞋.

p169.original: Consumable commodities, whether necessaries or luxuries, may be taxed in two different ways. The consumer may either pay an annual sum on account of his using or consuming goods of a certain kind; or the goods may be taxed while they remain in the hands of the dealer, and before they are delivered to the consumer. The consumable goods which last a considerable time before they are consumed altogether, are most properly taxed in the one way; those of which the consumption is either immediate or more speedy, in the other. The coach-tax and plate tax are examples of the former method of imposing; the greater part of the other duties of excise and customs, of the latter.
p169.zh: 消费性商品,无论是必要商品还是奢侈品,可以两种不同方式征税.消费者可以因其使用或消费某种商品而每年缴纳一笔款项;或者在商品仍由经销商掌握时,在交付消费者之前,对该商品征税。 在消费全部之前持续相当长时间的消耗性商品,以一种方式征税最为恰当;消费是立即的,或者更快的。教练员税和板税是前一种征收方法的例子;后者的消费税和关税的其他义务的较大部分。

p170.original: A coach may, with good management, last ten or twelve years. It might be taxed, once for all, before it comes out of the hands of the coach-maker. But it is certainly more convenient for the buyer to pay four pounds a-year for the privilege of keeping a coach, than to pay all at once forty or forty-eight pounds additional price to the coach-maker; or a sum equivalent to what the tax is likely to cost him during the time he uses the same coach. A service of plate in the same manner, may last more than a century. It is certainly-easier for the consumer to pay five shillings a-year for every hundred ounces of plate, near one per cent. of the value, than to redeem this long annuity at five-and-twenty or thirty years purchase, which would enhance the price at least five-and-twenty or thirty per cent. The different taxes which affect houses, are certainly more conveniently paid by moderate annual payments, than by a heavy tax of equal value upon the first building or sale of the house.
p170.zh: 教练在良好的管理下可以持续十年或十二年.可能要一劳永逸地征税,然后才从教练的手中出来. 但买主每年为保有教练员的特权支付4磅当然更方便,而不是一次性向教练员支付全部40或48磅的额外价格;或者相当于他使用同一教练员期间可能要缴纳的税款的金额.以同样方式为板块服务,可能持续一个多世纪.消费者每年为每100盎司的板块支付5先令,接近价值的1%,这当然是容易的,而不是以5年或30年的购买来赎回这一长年金,这至少会提高5年或30%的价格。影响住房的不同税额,当然更方便的是,通过适度的年薪支付,而不是通过对住房的首次建造或出售征收的等值的重税支付。

p171.original: It was the well-known proposal of Sir Matthew Decker, that all commodities, even those of which the consumption is either immediate or speedy, should be taxed in this manner; the dealer advancing nothing, but the consumer paying a certain annual sum for the licence to consume certain goods. The object of his scheme was to promote all the different branches of foreign trade, particularly the carrying trade, by taking away all duties upon importation and exportation, and thereby enabling the merchant to employ his whole capital and credit in the purchase of goods and the freight of ships, no part of either being diverted towards the advancing of taxes, The project, however, of taxing, in this manner, goods of immediate or speedy consumption, seems liable to the four following very important objections. First, the tax would be more unequal, or not so well proportioned to the expense and consumption of the different contributors, as in the way in which it is commonly imposed. The taxes upon ale, wine, and spiritous liquors, which are advanced by the dealers, are finally paid by the different consumers, exactly in proportion to their respective consumption. But if the tax were to be paid by purchasing a licence to drink those liquors, the sober would, in proportion to his consumption, be taxed much more heavily than the drunken consumer. A family which exercised great hospitality, would be taxed much more lightly than one who entertained fewer guests. Secondly, this mode of taxation, by paying for an annual, half-yearly, or quarterly licence to consume certain goods, would diminish very much one of the principal conveniences of taxes upon goods of speedy consumption; the piece-meal payment. In the price of threepence halfpenny, which is at present paid for a pot of porter, the different taxes upon malt, hops, and beer, together with the extraordinary profit which the brewer charges for having advanced than, may perhaps amount to about three halfpence. If a workman can conveniently spare those three halfpence, he buys a pot of porter. If he cannot, he contents himself with a pint; and, as a penny saved is a penny got, he thus gains a farthing by his temperance. He pays the tax piece-meal, as he can afford to pay it, and when he can afford to pay it, and every act of payment is perfectly voluntary, and what he can avoid if he chuses to do so. Thirdly, such taxes would operate less as sumptuary laws. When the licence was once purchased, whether the purchaser drunk much or drunk little, his tax would be the same. Fourthly, if a workman were to pay all at once, by yearly, half-yearly, or quarterly payments, a tax equal to what he at present pays, with little or no inconveniency, upon all the different pots and pints of porter which he drinks in any such period of time, the sum might frequently distress him very much. This mode of taxation, therefore, it seems evident, could never, without the most grievous oppression, produce a revenue nearly equal to what is derived from the present mode without any oppression. In several countries, however, commodities of an immediate or very speedy consumption are taxed in this manner. In Holland, people pay so much a-head for a licence to drink tea. I have already mentioned a tax upon bread, which, so far as it is consumed in farm houses and country villages, is there levied in the same manner.
p171.zh: 众所周知,马修·德克尔爵士建议,所有商品,即使是那些消费立即或迅速的商品,都应以这种方式征税;经销商一无所获,而是消费者每年支付一定数额的消费某些商品的许可证。 他的计划的目的是通过在进出口时取消所有关税,促进外贸的所有不同分支,特别是载货贸易,从而使商人能够利用全部资本和信贷购买货物和船运费,而其中任何一部分都不得转用于提高税收。 然而,以这种方式对立即或迅速消费的货物征税的项目似乎要受到以下四个非常重要的反对。 首先,税收将更加不平等,或者与不同缴款者的开支和消费比例不相称,就像通常征收的方式一样。 对酒类、酒类和烈性酒类的税收,由经销商推动,最终由不同的消费者支付,与其各自的消费成正比。 但是,如果通过购买饮酒许可证来支付税金,那么清醒者,按照他的消费比例,将比醉酒的消费者课税要重得多. 一个非常热情的家族,比一个招待较少的客人的家族,其税收要轻得多。 第二,这种征税方式每年、半年或每季度支付消费某些货物的许可证,将大大削弱对快速消费货物征税的主要便利之一,即一次销售。 目前,三便士半便士的价格是用来支付一壶搬运工的,对麦芽、大麻和啤酒的不同征税,加上酿酒商因比高而收取的超乎寻常的利润,可能相当于大约三便士。 如果一个工人能方便地放过这3个半便士,他就会买一壶搬运工. 如果他做不到,他就会用一品脱来充斥自己;而且,由于节省一分钱是得到一分钱的,因此他因脾气暴躁而获得一分钱。 他付税的零食,因为他能付得起,当他能付得起,每一次支付都是完全自愿的,如果他这样做,他可以避免什么。 第三,这种税收作为自发性法律的作用将减少。 当许可证一次购买时,无论购买者喝多了还是喝得很少,他的税收都是一样的. 第四,如果一个工人要一次一次地、每年、半年或每季度支付一笔相当于他目前所付的、很少或不方便的税,以支付他在任何这样一段时间内所饮的所有各种锅和酒,那么这笔钱可能经常使他感到非常不安。 因此,这种征税方式似乎很明显,没有最严重的压迫,就不可能产生几乎等于目前方式所得的收入,而没有任何压迫。 然而,在一些国家,即时或非常迅速消费的商品则以这种方式征税。 在荷兰,人们花这么多钱买喝茶的执照. 我已提到对面包的征税,就农场和乡村村庄的消费而言,这种征税也是以同样方式征收的。

p172.original: The duties of excise are imposed chiefly upon goods of home produce, destined for home consumption. They are imposed only upon a few sorts of goods of the most general use. There can never be any doubt, either concerning the goods which are subject to those duties, or concerning the particular duty which each species of goods is subject to. They fall almost altogether upon what I call luxuries, excepting always the four duties above mentioned, upon salt, soap, leather, candles, and perhaps that upon green glass.
p172.zh: 消费税主要针对家用产品,供家庭消费。 它们只用于几种最普遍使用的货物。绝不可对所应承担这些义务的货物或每一种类货物所应承担的特定义务有任何怀疑。 他们几乎完全依赖于我所说的奢侈品, 除了上述四项职责之外, 盐、肥皂、皮革、蜡烛, 以及绿色玻璃。

p173.original: The duties of customs are much more ancient than those of excise. They seem to have been called customs, as denoting customary payments, which had been in use for time immemorial. They appear to have been originally considered as taxes upon the profits of merchants. During the barbarous times of feudal anarchy, merchants, like all the other inhabitants of burghs, were considered as little better than emancipated bondmen, whose persons were despised, and whose gains were envied. The great nobility, who had consented that the king should tallage the profits of their own tenants, were not unwilling that he should tallage likewise those of an order of men whom it was much less their interest to protect. In those ignorant times, it was not understood, that the profits of merchants are a subject not taxable directly; or that the final payment of all such taxes must fall, with a considerable overcharge, upon the consumers.
p173.zh: 海关的关税远比货物税古老。 它们似乎被称为习俗,作为习惯付款的代号,而习惯付款是古老的。 它们最初似乎被认为是对商人利润的征税。 在封建无政府主义的野蛮时期,商人和布尔格人所有其他居民一样,被认为比解放的仆人好不到哪里去,他们的人被鄙视,他们的利益被羡慕.贵族们同意国王应该统计他们自己租户的利润,他们并不不愿意同样统计那些受他们保护的利益要小得多的男子的利润。 在那些无知的时代,人们不理解的是,商人的利润是不能直接征税的主体;或者,所有这类税收的最终支付必须落在消费者身上,而要向消费者收取相当高的超额费用。

p174.original: The gains of alien merchants were looked upon more unfavourably than those of English merchants. It was natural, therefore, that those of the former should be taxed more heavily than those of the latter. This distinction between the duties upon aliens and those upon English merchants, which was begun from ignorance, has been continued front the spirit of monopoly, or in order to give our own merchants an advantage, both in the home and in the foreign market.
p174.zh: 外国商人的所得比英国商人的得失更不讨好. 因此,对前者的征税应比后者的课税更重是自然的。 从无知开始的对外国人和对英国商人的义务之间的这种区分,继续以垄断精神为前列,或是为了在国内外市场给予我们自己的商人以优势。

p175.original: With this distinction, the ancient duties of customs were imposed equally upon all sorts of goods, necessaries as well its luxuries, goods exported as well as goods imported. Why should the dealers in one sort of goods, it seems to have been thought, be more favoured than those in another? or why should the merchant exporter be more favoured than the merchant importer?
p175.zh: 由于这种区别,古代的关税被平等征收到各种货物、必需品及其奢侈品、出口货物和进口货物。一种商品的经销商为什么比另一种商品的经销商更受青睐呢? 或者为什么商家出口商比商家进口商更受青睐呢?

p176.original: The ancient customs were divided into three branches. The first, and, perhaps, the most ancient of all those duties, was that upon wool and leather. It seems to have been chiefly or altogether an exportation duty. When the woollen manufacture came to be established in England, lest the king should lose any part of his customs upon wool by the exportation of woollen cloths, a like duty was imposed upon them. The other two branches were, first, a duty upon wine, which being imposed at so much a-ton, was called a tonnage; and, secondly, a duty upon all other goods, which being imposed at so much a-pound of their supposed value, was called a poundage. In the forty-seventh year of Edward III., a duty of sixpence in the pound was imposed upon all goods exported and imported, except wools, wool-felts, leather, and wines which were subject to particular duties. In the fourteenth of Richard II., this duty was raised to one shilling in the pound; but, three years afterwards, it was again reduced to sixpence. It was raised to eightpence in the second year of Henry IV.; and, in the fourth of the same prince, to one shilling. From this time to the ninth year of William III., this duty continued at one shilling in the pound. The duties of tonnage and poundage were generally granted to the king by one and the same act of parliament, and were called the subsidy of tonnage and poundage. The subsidy of poundage having continued for so long a time at one shilling in the pound, or at five per cent., a subsidy came, in the language of the customs, to denote a general duty of this kind of five per cent. This subsidy, which is now called the old subsidy, still continues to be levied, according to the book of rates established by the twelfth of Charles II. The method of ascertaining, by a book of rates, the value of goods subject to this duty, is said to be older than the time of James I. The new subsidy, imposed by the ninth and tenth of William III., was an additional five per cent. upon the greater part of goods. The one-third and the two-third subsidy made up between them another five per cent. of which they were proportionable parts. The subsidy of 1747 made a fourth five per cent. upon the greater part of goods; and that of 1759, a fifth upon some particular sorts of goods. Besides those five subsidies, a great variety of other duties have occasionally been imposed upon particular sorts of goods, in order sometimes to relieve the exigencie's of the state, and sometimes to regulate the trade of the country, according to the principles of the mercantile system.
p176.zh: 古代风俗分为三个分支.首先是羊毛和皮革,也许也是最古老的。 这似乎主要是或完全是出口义务。 当羊毛制品在英国建立时,以免国王因羊毛布的出口而失去羊毛上的任何一部分的风俗,对羊毛布也规定了类似的义务. 另外两个分支是:第一,对酒的征收义务,在如此多的一吨级时强制实行;第二,对所有其他商品的征收义务,以如此多的假定价值征收,则称为磅. 在爱德华三世的第四十七年,对所有进出口货物规定了六便士关税,但羊毛、羊毛、皮革和葡萄酒除外,它们都须承担特殊关税。 在理查二世的第十四世,这项义务被提高到英镑1先令;但是,三年之后,它再次被减少到6便士. 它在亨利四世的第二年被提升为八便士;在同一王子的第四年,升为一先令. 从这个时候到威廉三世九年,这项义务继续维持在英镑1先令的水平.吨位和磅位的义务一般由议会的同一法案授予国王,并称为吨位和磅位的补贴.英镑的补贴持续了很长时间,以英镑的一先令或5%计算。 用海关的语言来说,补贴意味着这种5%的一般义务。 根据查理二世十二世确定的费率书,现在称为旧补贴的这种补贴仍然继续征收. 据说,通过一本费率簿确定受这项义务约束的货物价值的方法比詹姆斯一世时代要老。威廉三世第九和第十世对大部分货物实行的新补贴是额外的5%。三分之一和三分之二的补贴在它们之间又构成5%,其中一部分是可分配的部分。1747年的补贴对大部分货物占四分之一,1759年的补贴对某些特定种类的货物占五分之一。 除了这五项补贴之外,偶尔还对特定种类的货物征收了各种各样的其他关税,有时是为了免除外出人的国税,有时是为了按照商贸制度的原则管理国家的贸易。

p177.original: That system has come gradually more and more into fashion. The old subsidy was imposed indifferently upon exportation, as well as importation. The four subsequent subsidies, as well as the other duties which have since been occasionally imposed upon particular sorts of goods, have, with a few exceptions, been laid altogether upon importation. The greater part of the ancient duties which had been imposed upon the exportation of the goods of home produce and manufacture, have either been lightened or taken away altogether. In most cases, they have been taken away. Bounties have even been given upon the exportation of some of them. Drawbacks, too, sometimes of the whole, and, in most cases, of a part of the duties which are paid upon the importation of foreign goods, have been granted upon their exportation. Only half the duties imposed by the old subsidy upon importation, are drawn back upon exportation; but the whole of those imposed by the latter subsidies and other imposts are, upon the greater parts of the goods, drawn back in the same manner. This growing favour of exportation, and discouragement of importation, have suffered only a few exceptions, which chiefly concern the materials of some manufactures. These our merchants and manufacturers are willing should come as cheap as possible to themselves, and as dear as possible to their rivals and competitors in other countries. Foreign materials are, upon this account, sometimes allowed to be imported duty-free; spanish wool, for example, flax, and raw linen yarn. The exportation of the materials of home produce, and of those which are the particular produce of our colonies, has sometimes been prohibited, and sometimes subjected to higher duties. The exportation of English wool has been prohibited. That of beaver skins, of beaver wool, and of gum-senega, has been subjected to higher duties; Great Britain, by the conquests of Canada and Senegal, having got almost the monopoly of those commodities.
p177.zh: 该系统已逐渐成为时尚。旧的补贴是对出口和进口不加区别的。 除了少数例外,后来的四项补贴以及后来偶尔对特定种类商品征收的其他税项,完全规定在进口时。出口家用产品和制造品的古老义务,有的被减轻,有的被完全夺走。在大多数情况下,他们都被带走。其中一些产品出口时甚至得到好处。出口外国货物时,也给予部分税款的拖欠,有时甚至多数情况下。旧的补贴对进口征收的关税只有一半在出口时收回;但后一种补贴和其他假货征收的全部关税在大部分商品上以同样的方式收回。 这种日益偏爱出口和抑制进口的情况只遇到少数例外,这主要涉及某些制成品的材料。 这些我们的商家和制造商们愿意尽可能低廉地为自己,尽可能地去珍视其他国家的对手和竞争对手.外国材料有时被允许免税进口;西班牙羊毛,例如麻,和原始亚麻线。出口家用产品以及作为我们殖民地特殊产品的材料有时受到禁止,有时还要承担更高的义务。禁止出口英国羊毛。 海狸皮、海狸羊毛和口香糖都承担了更高的义务;大不列颠,由于征服了加拿大和塞内加尔,几乎垄断了这些商品。

p178.original: That the mercantile system has not been very favourable to the revenue of the great body of the people, to the annual produce of the land and labour of the country, I have endeavoured to show in the fourth book of this Inquiry. It seems not to have been more favourable to the revenue of the sovereign; so far, at least, as that revenue depends upon the duties of customs.
p178.zh: 商贸制度对人民伟大身体的收入、对国家的土地和劳动力的年产量并不十分有利,我在本调查的第四本书中努力表明这一点。 它似乎没有更有利于主权国的收入;到目前为止,至少是因为这种收入取决于关税。

p179.original: In consequence of that system, the importation of several sorts of goods has been prohibited altogether. This prohibition has, in some cases, entirely prevented, and in others has very much diminished, the importation of those commodities, by reducing the importers to the necessity of smuggling. It has entirely prevented the importation of foreign wollens; and it has very much diminished that of foreign silks and velvets, In both cases, it has entirely annihilated the revenue of customs which might have been levied upon such importation.
p179.zh: 由于这一制度,几类货物的进口被完全禁止。在某些情况下,这种禁止使进口商减少走私的必要性,从而完全阻止了这些商品的进口,而在另一些情况下,这种禁止则大大减少了。 它完全阻止了外国软骨的进口;它大大降低了外国丝绸和丝绒的进口量,在这两种情况下,它完全摧毁了海关可能对这种进口征收的收入。

p180.original: The high duties which have been imposed upon the importation of many different sorts of foreign goods in order to discourage their consumption in Great Britain, have, in many cases, served only to encourage smuggling, and, in all cases, have reduced the revenues of the customs below what more moderate duties would have afforded. The saying of Dr. Swift, that in the arithmetic of the customs, two and two, instead of making four, make sometimes only one, holds perfectly true with regard to such heavy duties, which never could have been imposed, had not the mercantile system taught us, in many cases, to employ taxation as an instrument, not of revenue, but of monopoly.
p180.zh: 对进口许多不同种类的外国货物施加的高额关税,以阻止它们在大不列颠的消费,在许多情况下,这种高额关税只是鼓励走私,而且在所有情况下,海关收入都低于更温和的关税。医生的话斯威夫特,在计算风俗时,二和二,而不是四,有时只做一,对于这种不可能强加的重税,是完全正确的。 商贸制度在许多情况下没有教导我们把税收作为一种工具,而不是收入,而是垄断。

p181.original: The bounties which are sometimes given upon the exportation of home produce and manufactures, and the drawbacks which are paid upon the re-exportation of the greater part of foreign goods, have given occasion to many frauds, and to a species of smuggling, more destructive of the public revenue than any other. In order to obtain the bounty or drawback, the goods, it is well known, are sometimes shipped, and sent to sea, but soon afterwards clandestinely re-landed in some other part of the country. The defalcation of the revenue of customs occasioned by bounties and drawbacks, of which a great part are obtained fraudulently, is very great. The gross produce of the customs, in the year which ended on the 5th of January 1755, amounted to £5,068,000. The bounties which were paid out of this revenue, though in that year there was no bounty upon corn, amounted to £167,806. The drawbacks which were paid upon debentures and certificates, to £2,156,800. Bounties and drawbacks together amounted to £2,324,600. In consequence of these deductions, the revenue of the customs amounted only to £2,743,400; from which deducting £287,900 for the expense of management, in salaries and other incidents, the neat revenue of the customs for that year comes out to be £2,455,500. The expense of management, amounts, in this manner, to between five and six per cent. upon the gross revenue of the customs; and to something more than ten per cent. upon what remains of that revenue, after deducting what is paid away in bounties and drawbacks.
p181.zh: 有时在出口家用产品和制成品时得到的好处,以及大部分外国商品再出口时得到的缺点,都给许多欺诈行为和走私行为带来了机会,这些欺诈行为比任何其他行为都更加破坏公共收入。 为了获得赏金或缺点,货物,众所周知,有时被运出,然后被送上海,但不久之后又秘密地重新落地到该国其他地区。以欺诈手段获取大量收益和弊端的海关收入的解说非常出色。1755年1月5日结束的一年海关总产值为5,068,000英镑.这笔收入的丰收,虽然当年没有玉米的赏金,但达167 806英镑。向财产和证书支付的缺陷为2,156,800英镑。丰厚和缺点合计达2 324 600英镑。 由于这些扣除,海关的收入仅达2,743,400英镑;从中扣除287,900英镑的管理费用,在工资和其他事故方面,该年海关的整顿收入为2,455,500英镑。管理费用以这种方式从海关总收入中扣除了以利弊方式支付的金额,相当于5%至6%;从该收入中扣除了10%以上。

p182.original: Heavy duties being imposed upon almost all goods imported, our merchant importers smuggle as much, and make entry of as little as they can. Our merchant exporters, on the contrary, make entry of more than they export; sometimes out of vanity, and to pass for great dealers in goods which pay no duty gain a bounty back. Our exports, in consequence of these different frauds, appear upon the custom-house books greatly to overbalance our imports, to the unspeakable comfort of those politicians, who measure the national prosperity by what they call the balance of trade.
p182.zh: 对几乎所有进口货物征收重税,我国的商家进口商尽可能多地走私,尽量少地入境。 相反,我们的商家出口商的入境量超过出口量;有时出于虚荣,而让那些不缴税的大型商品商的入境又得到回报。 由于这些不同的欺诈行为,我们的出口出现在海关簿上,大大地使我国的进口量过度平衡,使那些政客感到难以言状的安慰,他们用所谓的贸易平衡来衡量国家繁荣。

p183.original: All goods imported, unless particularly exempted, and such exemptions are not very numerous, are liable to some duties of customs. If any goods are imported, not mentioned in the book of rates, they are taxed at 4s:9¾d. for every twenty shillings value, according to the oath of the importer, that is, nearly at five subsidies, or five poundage duties. The book of rates is extremely comprehensive, and enumerates a great variety of articles, many of them little used, and, therefore, not well known. It is, upon this account, frequently uncertain under what article a particular sort of goods ought to be classed, and, consequently what duty they ought to pay. Mistakes with regard to this sometimes ruin the custom-house officer, and frequently occasion much trouble, expense, and vexation to the importer. In point of perspicuity, precision, and distinctness, therefore, the duties of customs are much inferior to those of excise.
p183.zh: 所有进口货物,除非特别豁免,以及此类豁免数量不多,都须缴纳某些关税。 如果进口任何货物,在税率簿中未提及,则按照进口商的宣誓,每20先令价值,即将近5项补贴,或5英镑税,按每20先令4:93⁄4日征税。费率之书极为全面,列举的文章种类繁多,其中很多很少被使用,因此并不广为人知. 因此,常常无法确定某一类货物应属于哪一条,因此,它们应承担什么义务。这方面的错误有时会破坏海关官员,经常给进口商带来很多麻烦、开支和烦恼。 因此,从纯度、精确度和独特性来看,关税远低于消费税。

p184.original: In order that the greater part of the members of any society should contribute to the public revenue, in proportion to their respective expense, it does not seem necessary that every single article of that expense should be taxed. The revenue which is levied by the duties of excise is supposed to fall as equally upon the contributors as that which is levied by the duties of customs; and the duties of excise are imposed upon a few articles only of the most general used and consumption. It has been the opinion of many people, that, by proper management, the duties of customs might likewise, without any loss to the public revenue, and with great advantage to foreign trade, be confined to a few articles only.
p184.zh: 为了让任何社会的大部分成员按照各自开支的比例为公共收入缴款,似乎没有必要对这笔开支的每一个条款征税。消费税征收的收入应与关税征收的收入一样,由缴款者承担;消费税只征收最普通的消费税。许多人认为,通过适当的管理,海关的关税同样可以不损失任何公共收入,对对外贸易也有很大好处,但仅限于少数条款。

p185.original: The foreign articles, of the most general use and consumption in Great Britain, seem at present to consist chiefly in foreign wines and brandies; in some of the productions of America and the West Indies, sugar, rum, tobacco, cocoa-nuts, etc. and in some of those of the East Indies, tea, coffee, china-ware, spiceries of all kinds, several sorts of piece-goods, etc. These different articles afford, the greater part of the perhaps, at present, revenue which is drawn from the duties of customs. The taxes which at present subsist upon foreign manufactures, if you except those upon the few contained in the foregoing enumeration, have, the greater part of them, been imposed for the purpose, not of revenue, but of monopoly, or to give our own merchants an advantage in the home market. By removing all prohibitions, and by subjecting all foreign manufactures to such moderate taxes, as it was found from experience, afforded upon each article the greatest revenue to the public, our own workmen might still have a considerable advantage in the home market; and many articles, some of which at present afford no revenue to government, and others a very inconsiderable one, might afford a very great one.
p185.zh: 外国文章,在大不列颠最普遍使用和消费,目前似乎主要包括外国葡萄酒和白兰地;在美国和西印度群岛的一些产品中,有糖,朗姆酒,烟草,可可核等,东印度群岛的一些产品中,有茶,咖啡,瓷器,各种香料,几种零碎商品等. 这些不同条款提供了目前可能从关税中提取的大部分收入。外国制成品目前所承受的税收,如果除上述所列少数产品外,主要是为了收入目的,而是为了垄断目的,或者为了使我们自己的商人在母国市场上享有优势。 通过取消所有禁令,并对所有外国制造品征收从经验中发现的、给每一条带来最大收入的中等税率,我们自己的工人在国内市场仍然可能拥有相当大的优势;许多物品,其中一些目前没有给政府带来收入,而另一些则是一个非常不值得考虑的物品,可能负担很大。

p186.original: High taxes, sometimes by diminishing the consumption of the taxed commodities, and sometimes by encouraging smuggling frequently afford a smaller revenue to government than what might be drawn from more moderate taxes.
p186.zh: 高税收,有时是减少被征税商品的消费,有时是鼓励走私,往往比从较温和的税收中获取的收入为政府提供较少的收入。

p187.original: When the diminution of revenue is the effect of the diminution of consumption, there can be but one remedy, and that is the lowering of the tax. When the diminution of revenue is the effect of the encouragement given to smuggling, it may, perhaps, be remedied in two ways; either by diminishing the temptation to smuggle, or by increasing the difficulty of smuggling. The temptation to smuggle can be diminished only by the lowering of the tax; and the difficulty of smuggling can be increased only by establishing that system of administration which is most proper for preventing it.
p187.zh: 当收入减少是消费减少的影响时,只能有一个补救办法,那就是降低税收。 如果收入减少是鼓励走私的结果,也许可以采取两种方式加以补救:减少走私的诱惑,或增加走私的难度。 只有降低税收,才能减少走私的诱惑;只有建立最适于防止走私的行政制度,才能增加走私的难度。

p188.original: The excise laws, it appears, I believe, from experience, obstruct and embarrass the operations of the smuggler much more effectually than those of the customs. By introducing into the customs a system of administration as similar to that of the excise as the nature of the different duties will admit, the difficulty of smuggling might be very much increased. This alteration, it has been supposed by many people, might very easily be brought about.
p188.zh: 我认为,从经验来看,消费法比海关法律更能有效地阻碍和羞辱走私者的活动。 通过在海关实行一种类似于不同关税性质所承认货物消费的管理制度,走私的困难可能大大增加。许多人认为这种改变是很容易实现的。

p189.original: The importer of commodities liable to any duties of customs, it has been said, might, at his option, be allowed either to carry them to his own private warehouse; or to lodge them in a warehouse, provided either at his own expense or at that of the public, but under the key of the custom-house officer, and never to be opened but in his presence. If the merchant carried them to his own private warehouse, the duties to be immediately paid, and never afterwards to be drawn back; and that warehouse to be at all times subject to the visit and examination of the custom-house officer, in order to ascertain how far the quantity contained in it corresponded with that for which the duty had been paid. If he carried them to the public warehouse, no duty to be paid till they were taken out for home consumption. If taken out for exportation, to be duty-free; proper security being always given that they should be so exported. The dealers in those particular commodities, either by wholesale or retail, to be at all times subject to the visit and examination of the custom-house officer; and to be obliged to justify, by proper certificates, the payment of the duty upon the whole quantity contained in their shops or warehouses. What are called the excise duties upon rum imported, are at present levied in this manner; and the same system of administration might, perhaps, be extended to all duties upon goods imported; provided always that those duties were, like the duties of excise, confined to a few sorts of goods of the most general use and consumption. If they were extended to almost all sorts of goods, as at present, public warehouses of sufficient extent could not easily be provided; and goods of a very delicate nature, or of which the preservation required much care and attention, could not safely be trusted by the merchant in any warehouse but his own.
p189.zh: 据说,应征任何关税的商品的进口商,可自行选择将其运至自己的私人仓库;或将其存放在仓库内,由他本人或公众自费提供,但由海关官员按键提供,而且从不开放,只有他在场。 如果商人将货物运至自己的私人仓库,应立即支付有关责任,以后再不提取;该仓库随时都要接受海关官员的视察和检查,以便确定所载数量与已支付该义务的数量相符。 如果他把它们带到公共仓库,在带他们出家用之前,不支付任何费用。 如果出口,则免税;始终给予适当的安全,即出口。 这些特定商品的经销商,无论是批发还是零售,在任何时候都须接受海关官员的检查和检查;并有义务通过适当的证明证明,证明其商店或仓库内全部货款的支付是合理的。 目前,对进口朗姆酒征收所谓的消费税就是以这种方式征收的;同样的管理制度也许可以扩大到对进口货物征收的所有税;只要这些税与消费税一样,始终限于几种最普遍使用和消费的货物。 如果象目前那样将其扩大到几乎所有种类的货物,那么不可能轻易地提供足够规模的公共仓库;而且非常微妙或保存需要大量注意和注意的货物,商人不可能安全地在任何仓库中信任他,除非他自己的仓库。

p190.original: If, by such a system of administration, smuggling to any considerable extent could be prevented, even under pretty high duties; and if every duty was occasionally either heightened or lowered according as it was most likely, either the one way or the other, to afford the greatest revenue to the state; taxation being always employed as an instrument of revenue, and never of monopoly; it seems not improbable that a revenue, at least equal to the present neat revenue of the customs, might be drawn from duties upon the importation of only a few sorts of goods of the most general use and consumption; and that the duties of customs might thus be brought to the same degree of simplicity, certainty, and precision, as those of excise. What the revenue at present loses by drawbacks upon the re-exportation of foreign goods, which are afterwards re-landed and consumed at home, would, under this system, be saved altogether. If to this saving, which would alone be very considerable, were added the abolition of all bounties upon the exportation of home produce; in all cases in which those bounties were not in reality drawbacks of some duties of excise which had before been advanced; it cannot well be doubted, but that the neat revenue of customs might, after an alteration of this kind, be fully equal to what it had ever been before.
p190.zh: 如果通过这种行政制度,可以相当程度地防止走私,即使有相当高的关税;如果每一税额偶尔会增加或降低,因为无论哪种方式都最有可能给国家带来最大的收入;税收总是作为收入工具,从不具有垄断性;似乎不可能从仅进口几种最普遍使用和消费的商品的关税中提取至少等于海关目前整洁收入的收入;因此,关税可以与消费税一样,达到简单、确定和精确的程度。 根据这一制度,外国货物在重新出口后重新落地并在国内消费,现在由于出现不利因素而损失的收入将全部节省下来。 如果在仅是相当可观的节省之外,还要取消出口家用产品时的所有好处;在所有情况下,这些好处实际上并非是以前征收的某些消费税的缺点;这不容置疑,但海关的整顿收入在这种改变之后可能与以前完全相等。

p191.original: If, by such a change of system, the public revenue suffered no loss, the trade and manufactures of the country would certainly gain a very considerable advantage. The trade in the commodities not taxed, by far the greatest number would be perfectly free, and might be carried on to and from all parts of the world with every possible advantage. Among those commodities would be comprehended all the necessaries of life, and all the materials of manufacture. So far as the free importation of the necessaries of life reduced their average money price in the home market, it would reduce the money price of labour, but without reducing in any respect its real recompence. The value of money is in proportion to the quantity of the necessaries of life which it will purchase. That of the necessaries of life is altogether independent of the quantity of money which can be had for them. The reduction in the money price of labour would necessarily be attended with a proportionable one in that of all home manufactures, which would thereby gain some advantage in all foreign markets. The price of some manufactures would be reduced, in a still greater proportion, by the free importation of the raw materials. If raw silk could be imported from China and Indostan, duty-free, the silk manufacturers in England could greatly undersell those of both France and Italy. There would be no occasion to prohibit the importation of foreign silks and velvets. The cheapness of their goods would secure to our own workmen, not only the possession of a home, but a very great command of the foreign market. Even the trade in the commodities taxed, would be carried on with much more advantage than at present. If those commodities were delivered out of the public warehouse for foreign exportation, being in this case exempted from all taxes, the trade in them would be perfectly free. The carrying trade, in all sorts of goods, would, under this system, enjoy every possible advantage. If these commodities were delivered out for home consumption, the importer not being obliged to advance the tax till he had an opportunity of selling his goods, either to some dealer, or to some consumer, he could always afford to sell them cheaper than if he had been obliged to advance it at the moment of importation. Under the same taxes, the foreign trade of consumption, even in the taxed commodities, might in this manner be carried on with much more advantage than it is at present.
p191.zh: 如果通过这种体制的改变,公共收入不会遭受损失,那么该国的贸易和制造业肯定会获得相当大的好处。 未征税的商品贸易迄今数量最多,是完全自由的,可能以一切可能的优势进入和离开世界各地。 在这些商品中,将理解生命的所有必要条件和所有制造材料。 只要生活必需品的自由进口降低了他们在家庭市场上的平均货币价格,就可降低劳动力的货币价格,但无论如何不会降低其真正的回报。货币价值与其购买的生命必需品的数量成正比。生活必需品完全独立于他们可以拥有的资金数量。劳动力货币价格的降低必须在所有家用制成品中以可分配的比例进行,从而在所有外国市场中获得一定的优势。 一些制成品的价格将因原料的自由进口而降低,比例更高。 如果从中国和免税的印度斯坦进口生丝,英国的丝绸制造商可以大大低于法国和意大利的丝绸。 没有机会禁止进口外国丝绸和丝绒。 他们的商品的便宜,能保证我们自己的工人,不但拥有一个住宅,而且能够非常大地指挥外国市场.即使是被征税的商品贸易,也将比现在更有利。 如果这些商品从公共仓库运出,供出口,在这种情况下,免除所有税,则这些商品的贸易是完全自由的。 在这一制度下,各种货物的承载贸易将享有一切可能的优势。 如果这些商品被运出供家庭消费,进口商在有机会将其货物出售给某个经销商或一些消费者之前,没有义务提前缴纳税款,那么,他总是比在进口时被迫提前出售更便宜。 根据同样的税收,对外消费贸易,即使是在已征税的商品中,可能以这种方式进行,其优势比目前要大得多。

p192.original: It was the object of the famous excise scheme of Sir Robert Walpole, to establish, with regard to wine and tobacco, a system not very unlike that which is here proposed. But though the bill which was then brought into Parliament, comprehended those two commodities only, it was generally supposed to be meant as an introduction to a more extensive scheme of the same kind. Faction, combined with the interest of smuggling merchants, raised so violent, though so unjust a clamour, against that bill, that the minister thought proper to drop it; and, from a dread of exciting a clamour of the same kind, none of his successors have dared to resume the project.
p192.zh: 罗伯特·瓦尔波尔爵士著名的消费计划的目的是,在葡萄酒和烟草方面,建立一个与这里提出的制度不甚相似的制度。 但是,尽管后来提交议会的法案只理解这两种商品,但一般认为该法案是提出一种更广泛的同类计划。派别与走私商人的利益一道,激起如此暴力,尽管如此不公正的呼喊,反对该法案,使部长认为应该放弃该法案;并且,由于害怕令人激动的同一种呼喊,他的继任者都不敢恢复该项目。

p193.original: The duties upon foreign luxuries, imported for home consumption, though they sometimes fall upon the poor, fall principally upon people of middling or more than middling fortune. Such are, for example, the duties upon foreign wines, upon coffee, chocolate, tea, sugar, etc.
p193.zh: 对外国奢侈品征收关税,用于家庭消费,虽然有时落在穷人身上,但主要落在居家居家或居家居家居家的人身上。 例如,外国葡萄酒、咖啡、巧克力、茶叶、糖等的关税。

p194.original: The duties upon the cheaper luxuries of home produce, destined for home consumption, fall pretty equally upon people of all ranks, in proportion to their respective expense. The poor pay the duties upon malt, hops, beer, and ale, upon their own consumption; the rich, upon both their own consumption and that of their servants.
p194.zh: 家庭产品廉价奢侈品的消费费用,按其开支比例,对各阶层的人来说,都相当容易负担。穷人自己消费麦芽、大麻、啤酒和啤酒,富人自己消费和仆人的消费,都支付关税。

p195.original: The whole consumption of the inferior ranks of people, or of those below the middling rank, it must be observed, is, in every country, much greater, not only in quantity, but in value, than that of the middling, and of those above the middling rank. The whole expense of the inferior is much greater titan that of the superior ranks. In the first place, almost the whole capital of every country is annually distributed among the inferior ranks of people, as the wages of productive labour. Secondly, a great part of the revenue, arising from both the rent of land and the profits of stock, is annually distributed among the same rank, in the wages and maintenance of menial servants, and other unproductive labourers. Thirdly, some part of the profits of stock belongs to the same rank, as a revenue arising from the employment of their small capitals. The amount of the profits annually made by small shopkeepers, tradesmen, and retailers of all kinds, is everywhere very considerable, and makes a very considerable portion of the annual produce. Fourthly and lastly, some part even of the rent of land belongs to the same rank; a considerable part to those who are somewhat below the middling rank, and a small part even to the lowest rank; common labourers sometimes possessing in property an acre or two of land. Though the expense of those inferior ranks of people, therefore, taking them individually, is very small, yet the whole mass of it, taking them collectively, amounts always to by much the largest portion of the whole expense of the society; what remains of the annual produce of the land and labour of the country, for the consumption of the superior ranks, being always much less, not only in quantity, but in value. The taxes upon expense, therefore, which fall chiefly upon that of the superior ranks of people, upon the smaller portion of the annual produce, are likely to be much less productive than either those which fall indifferently upon the expense of all ranks, or even those which fall chiefly upon that of the inferior ranks, than either those which fall indifferently upon the whole annual produce, or those which fall chiefly upon the larger portion of it. The excise upon the materials and manufacture of home-made fermented and spirituous liquors, is, accordingly, of all the different taxes upon expense, by far the most productive; and this branch of the excise falls very much, perhaps principally, upon the expense of the common people. In the year which ended on the 5th of July 1775, the gross produce of this branch of the excise amounted to £3,341,837:9:9.
p195.zh: 必须看到,在每个国家,低等人群或低等人群的全部消费,不仅在数量上,而且在价值上,都比低等人群和低等人群的消费要大得多。下层人的全部费用 比上层人要大得多 首先,几乎每个国家的首都每年都作为生产性劳动力的工资在低层人群中分配。 第二,每年有很大一部分收入来自土地租金和股票利润,这些收入在同级人员、男仆和其他非生产性工人的工资和维持费中分配。 三,股票的利润部分属于同级,作为受雇于其小都城产生的收入. 小店主、商人和各种零售商每年赚取的利润数额在任何地方都非常可观,并且占年度产量的相当大一部分。 第四,也是最后一点,土地租金中有些部分属于同一等级;相当一部分属于低于居低级的人,一小部分甚至属于最低级的人;普通工人有时拥有一亩或两亩土地的财产。 虽然这些低等阶层人民的开支,因此,单独地把他们带走,是很小的,但是,他们作为一个整体,其全部开支总是占社会全部开支的最大部分;国家土地和劳动力的年产量所剩无几,用于上等阶层的消费,总要少得多,不仅数量,而且价值。 因此,费用税主要由上层人民承担,年产比重较小,其生产力可能大大低于各级各阶层无所顾忌的费用,甚至低于下层各阶层的税收,而低于整个年产无所顾忌的税收,或低于大部分年产。 因此,自制发酵和烈性酒的材料和制造的消费是迄今各种费用税中最有成效的;消费的这一分支可能主要落在普通人民身上。 在1775年7月5日结束的一年中,这个分支的消费总产值达到3,341,837:9:9.

p196.original: It must always be remembered, however, that it is the luxuries, and not the necessary expense of the inferior ranks of people, that ought ever to be taxed. The final payment of any tax upon their necessary expense, would fall altogether upon the superior ranks of people; upon the smaller portion of the annual produce, and not upon the greater. Such a tax must, in all cases, either raise the wages of labour, or lessen the demand for it. It could not raise the wages of labour, without throwing the final payment of the tax upon the superior ranks of people. It could not lessen the demand for labour, without lessening the annual produce of the land and labour of the country, the fund upon which all taxes must be finally paid. Whatever might be the state to which a tax of this kind reduced the demand for labour, it must always raise wages higher than they otherwise would be in that state; and the final payment of this enhancement of wages must, in all cases, fall upon the superior ranks of people.
p196.zh: 然而,必须永远记住,应该征税的应该是奢侈的阶层,而不是低等阶层的必要开支。任何税收的最后支付都取决于其必要的开支,完全取决于高阶层的人;取决于年产量的较小部分,而不是更大的部分。在任何情况下,这种税必须提高劳动工资或减少对劳动工资的需求。 它不能提高劳动工资,不把最后的税款交给上级人员。 它不能减少对劳动力的需求,除非减少该国土地和劳动力的年产量,而这是所有税收最终都必须缴纳的基金。 无论这种税项对哪个州减少了对劳动力的需求,它必须总是提高工资,而工资的提高最终必须取决于人民的上级。

p197.original: Fermented liquors brewed, and spiritous liquors distilled, not for sale, but for private use, are not in Great Britain liable to any duties of excise. This exemption, of which the object is to save private families from the odious visit and examination of the tax-gatherer, occasions the burden of those duties to fall frequently much lighter upon the rich than upon the poor. It is not, indeed, very common to distil for private use, though it is done sometimes. But in the country, many middling and almost all rich and great families, brew their own beer. Their strong beer, therefore, costs them eight shillings a-barrel less than it costs the common brewer, who must have his profit upon the tax, as well as upon all the other expense which he advances. Such families, therefore, must drink their beer at least nine or ten shillings a-barrel cheaper than any liquor of the same quality can be drank by the common people, to whom it is everywhere more convenient to buy their beer, by little and little, from the brewery or the ale-house. Malt, in the same manner, that is made for the use of a private family, is not liable to the visit or examination of the tax-gatherer but, in this case the family must compound at seven shillings and sixpence a-head for the tax. Seven shillings and sixpence are equal to the excise upon ten bushels of malt; a quantity fully equal to what all the different members of any sober family, men, women, and children, are, at an average, likely to consume. But in rich and great families, where country hospitality is much practised, the malt liquors consumed by the members of the family make but a small part of the consmnption of the house. Either on account of this composition, however, or for other reasons, it is not near so common to malt as to brew for private use. It is difficult to imagine any equitable reason, why those who either brew or distil for private use should not be subject to a composition of the same kind.
p197.zh: 酿造的发酵酒和蒸馏的烈酒,不是供出售,而是供私人使用,在英国不承担任何消费义务。 这种免除的目的是使私人家庭免于对税收征收者的恶毒探访和检查,因此,这种免除往往使富人的负担比穷人的负担轻得多。 虽然有时可以提取,供私人使用,但实际上并不常见。 但在国内,许多杂工 和几乎所有的富裕和伟大的家庭, 酿造自己的啤酒。 因此,他们的强力啤酒比普通酿酒商少花费8先令一桶,后者必须靠税收和他所垫付的所有其他费用获得利润。 因此,这些家庭必须至少喝9或10先令一桶的啤酒,比普通人喝任何同样质量的酒都要便宜,因为任何地方都更方便从酿酒厂或啤酒厂购买啤酒。以同样方式,为私人家庭所用,不需对征税人进行探视或检查,但在这种情况下,家庭必须增加7先令和6便士的税额。 七先令和六便士等于麦芽酒十种灌木的消费;其数量完全等于任何清醒家庭的所有不同成员,不论男女老幼,平均来说都可能消费多少。 但是在富裕和伟大的家庭里, 乡村的招待活动很多, 家庭成员饮用的麦芽酒只是房子的一小部分。 然而,由于这种成分或其他原因,麦芽酒并非太常见,也并非太常见于酿酒供私人使用。很难想象有什么公平的理由,为什么那些酿造或提取供私人使用的人不应受到同样种类的构成的约束。

p198.original: A greater revenue than what is at present drawn from all the heavy taxes upon malt, beer, and ale, might be raised, it has frequently been said, by a much lighter tax upon malt; the opportunities of defrauding the revenue being much greater in a brewery than in a malt-house; and those who brew for private use being exempted from all duties or composition for duties, which is not the case with those who malt for private use.
p198.zh: 与目前从对麦芽、啤酒和啤酒的所有重税中提取的收入相比,收入可能增加,人们经常说,对麦芽征收的税要轻得多;在酿酒厂中诈骗收入的机会比在麦芽院中要大得多;为私人用途酿酒的人免征所有关税或关税组成,而对于为私人用途而酿酒的人则不然。

p199.original: In the porter brewery of London, a quarter of malt is commonly brewed into more than two barrels and a-half, sometimes into three barrels of porter. The different taxes upon malt amount to six shillings a-quarter; those upon strong ale and beer to eight shillings a-barrel. In the porter brewery, therefore, the different taxes upon malt, beer, and ale, amount to between twenty-six and thirty shillings upon the produce of a quarter of malt. In the country brewery for common country sale, a quarter of malt is seldom brewed into less than two barrels of strong, and one barrel of small beer; frequently into two barrels and a-half of strong beer. The different taxes upon small beer amount to one shilling and fourpence a-barrel. In the country brewery, therefore, the different taxes upon malt, beer, and ale, seldom amount to less than twenty-three shillings and fourpence, frequently to twenty-six shillings, upon the produce of a quarter of malt. Taking the whole kingdom at an average, therefore, the whole amount of the duties upon malt, beer, and ale, cannot be estimated at less than twenty-four or twenty-five shillings upon the produce of a quarter of malt. But by taking off all the different duties upon beer and ale, and by trebling the malt tax, or by raising it from six to eighteen shilling's upon the quarter of malt, a greater revenue, it is said, might be raised by this single tax, than what is at present drawn from all those heavier taxes.
p199.zh: 在伦敦的搬运工酿酒厂中,四分之一的麦芽通常被酿成两桶半以上,有时会酿成三桶的搬运工. 对麦芽的不同税额为每季6先令;烈酒和啤酒的税额为每桶8先令。 因此,在搬运工酿酒厂,对麦芽、啤酒和啤酒的不同征税在四分之一麦芽的产物上为26至30先令。在该国,用于共同销售的酿酒厂,四分之一的麦芽很少酿成不到两桶强酒,一桶小啤酒;经常酿成两桶半强啤酒。 对小啤酒的不同征税额为一先令和四便士一桶。 因此,在国内酿酒厂,对麦芽、啤酒和啤酒的不同征税很少达到不到23先令和4便士,通常达到26先令,在生产四分之一麦芽时。 因此,以整个王国平均计算,对于麦芽、啤酒和啤酒的全部责任,在四分之一麦芽的产物上,不能估计不到24或25先令。 但是,通过脱下啤酒和啤酒上的所有不同关税,通过加倍征收麦芽税,或者通过在麦芽季度从六先令提高到十八先令,可以说,通过这一单项税收,可能比目前从所有那些较重的税收中提取的税收增加更多的收入。

p200.original: In 1772, the old malt tax produced......... £722,023: 11: 11 The additional... £356,776: 7: 9¾ In 1775, the old tax produced............... £561,627: 3: 7½ The additional... £278,650: 15: 3¾ In 1774, the old tax produced ............ £624,614: 17: 5¾ The additional....£310,745: 2: 8½ In 1775, the old tax produced ............£657,357: 0: 8¼ The additional....£323,785: 12: 6¼ £5,855,580: 12: 0¾ Average of these four years .............. £958,895: 3: 0

p201.original: In 1772, the country excise produced.......£1,243,120: 5: 3 The London brewery 408,260: 7: 2¾ In 1773, the country excise................£1,245,808: 3: 3 The London brewery 405,406: 17: 10½ In 1774, the country excise................£1,246,373: 14: 5½ The London brewery 320,601: 18: 0¼ In 1775, the country excise................£1,214,583: 6: 1¼ The London brewery 463,670: 7: 0¼ 4)£6,547,832: 19: 2¼ Average of these four years ..............£1,636,958: 4: 9½ To which adding the average malt tax........ 958,895: 3: 0¼

p202.original: The whole amount of those different taxes comes out to be........£2,595,835: 7: 10
p202.zh: 这些不同税项的总额是... 2 595 835英镑: 7: 10

p203.original: But, by trebling the malt tax, or by raising it from six to eighteen shillings upon the quarter of malt, that single tax would produce.....£2,876,685: 9: 0 A sum which exceeds the foregoing by.... 280,832: 1: 3
p203.zh: 但是,通过将麦芽税翻倍,或者在麦芽季度从6先令提高到18先令,单一的税将产生...2,876,685英镑:9:0,超过前述的金额通过.280,832: 1: 3 (简体中文).

p204.original: Under the old malt tax, indeed, is comprehended a tax of four shillings upon the hogshead of cyder, and another of ten shillings upon the barrel of mum. In 1774, the tax upon cyder produced only £3,083:6:8. It probably fell somewhat short of its usual amount; all the different taxes upon cyder, having, that year, produced less than ordinary. The tax upon mum, though much heavier, is still less productive, on account of the smaller consumption of that liquor. But to balance whatever may be the ordinary amount of those two taxes, there is comprehended under what is called the country excise, first, the old excise of six shillings and eightpence upon the hogshead of cyder; secondly, a like tax of six shillings and eightpence upon the hogshead of verjuice; thirdly, another of eight shillings and ninepence upon the hogshead of vinegar; and, lastly, a fourth tax of elevenpence upon the gallon of mead or metheglin.
